articles.title: How deep-rooted medical bias creates deadly consequences for addiction patients
articles.summary: Addiction treatments are safe, effective — and rarely offered to patients. That's because many doctors and nurses still view people with alcohol or drug addiction with suspicion and hostility.
articles.titleZh: 根深蒂固的医学偏见如何给成瘾患者造成致命后果
articles.summaryZh: 成瘾治疗是安全、有效的，但很少提供给患者。这是因为许多医生和护士仍然对酗酒或吸毒成瘾的人抱有怀疑和敌意。

contentParagraphs.en: In bodycam footage released by the Milwaukie Police Department, 26-year-old Jean Descamps can be seen in a hospital bed at the Providence Milwaukie Hospital emergency room in Milwaukie, Ore., in December 2023. Soon after he was discharged by the hospital, Descamps died from drugs already in his system.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2023 年 12 月，在密尔沃基警察局发布的随身摄像机镜头中，可以看到 26 岁的让·德坎普斯 (Jean Descamps) 躺在俄勒冈州密尔沃基市普罗维登斯密尔沃基医院急诊室的病床上。出院后不久，德坎普斯就因体内已有药物死亡。

contentParagraphs.en: Milwaukie Police Department/Screenshot by NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局/NPR 截图

contentParagraphs.en: Milwaukie Police Department/Screenshot by NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局/NPR 截图

contentParagraphs.en: On a cold December night in 2023, the staff at Providence Milwaukie Hospital in Milwaukie, Ore., called local police. They wanted help getting one of their patients, a 26-year-old man named Jean Descamps, out of the emergency room.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2023 年 12 月一个寒冷的夜晚，俄勒冈州密尔沃基市普罗维登斯密尔沃基医院的工作人员报了当地警方。他们希望有人帮助他们的一名病人（26 岁，名叫让·德坎普斯）离开急诊室。

contentParagraphs.en: "He's been evaluated medically. There's no medical problems for him," a member of the hospital team, who NPR has not been able to identify, told police. The moment was captured on an officer's body camera.
contentParagraphs.zh: “他已经接受了医学评估。他没有任何健康问题，”一名医院团队成员告诉警方，该团队成员的身份尚未得到美国公共广播电台的确认。这一刻被一名警官的随身摄像机拍了下来。

contentParagraphs.en: Records show the hospital's medical staff believed Descamps — emaciated, covered in feces, and often unresponsive — was experiencing symptoms of chronic street drug use, a leading cause of death for young Americans.
contentParagraphs.zh: 记录显示，医院的医务人员认为，德坎普斯身体消瘦，浑身是粪便，而且常常反应迟钝，他正在经历长期街头吸毒的症状，这是美国年轻人死亡的主要原因。

contentParagraphs.en: After Descamps arrived in an ambulance earlier that day, hospital staff cleaned him up and administered naloxone, a medication that reverses opioid overdoses. But now they wanted him gone. "He's not thriving chronically, but there's no medical reason for him to be here anymore," one hospital staffer can be heard saying.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当天早些时候，德坎普乘坐救护车抵达后，医院工作人员为他进行了清理，并服用了纳洛酮，这是一种可以逆转阿片类药物过量的药物。但现在他们希望他离开。一名医院工作人员说道：“他的长期健康状况不佳，但没有任何医学理由让他再留在这里。”

contentParagraphs.en: Video released by the Milwaukie Police Department shows Descamps sprawled in a hospital bed, his body limp, moaning and drooling, while medical staff stood nearby. After determining Descamps was too unwell to spend the night in jail, police officers challenged the hospital's decision to discharge him.
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局发布的视频显示，德坎普斯躺在医院的病床上，身体瘫软，呻吟着，流着口水，医护人员就站在附近。在确定德坎普斯身体状况太差而无法在监狱里过夜后，警察对医院让他出院的决定提出了质疑。

contentParagraphs.en: "He can't be on his own," one officer said. "Why is he being released? We have no place to take him."
contentParagraphs.zh: “他不能独自一人，”一名警官说。 “为什么要释放他？我们没有地方可以收容他。”

contentParagraphs.en: "A bus station is fine," a hospital worker replied. Another member of the hospital staff told police Descamps was faking the severity of his illness: "It's not really a medical problem, it's malingering."
contentParagraphs.zh: “公交车站就可以。”一名医院工作人员回答道。医院的另一名工作人员告诉警方，德坎普斯伪造了自己病情的严重程度：“这并不是真正的医疗问题，而是装病。”

contentParagraphs.en: Officers eventually complied, rolling Descamps' limp body in a wheelchair into the dark parking lot, where they covered him with a blanket against the winter cold. Police who gathered around Descamps can be heard voicing fear for his safety.
contentParagraphs.zh: 警察最终答应了，将轮椅上的德坎普斯瘫软的身体推到黑暗的停车场，并给他盖上了毯子以抵御冬天的寒冷。可以听到聚集在德坎普周围的警察对他的安全表示担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: In video footage released by the Milwaukie Police Department, an officer can be seen rolling Descamps in a wheelchair to exit the hospital emergency room. "Do you feel at all comfortable with anything that's going on right now?" one police officer asked. Another officer answered, "No."
contentParagraphs.zh: 在密尔沃基警察局发布的视频片段中，可以看到一名警官推着轮椅上的德坎普离开医院急诊室。 “你对现在发生的事情感到舒服吗？”一名警官问道。另一名军官回答：“没有。”

contentParagraphs.en: Milwaukie Police Department/Screenshot by NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局/NPR 截图

contentParagraphs.en: Milwaukie Police Department/Screenshot by NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局/NPR 截图

contentParagraphs.en: "Do you feel at all comfortable with anything that's going on right now?" one police officer asked. Another officer answered, "No."
contentParagraphs.zh: “你对现在发生的事情感到舒服吗？”一名警官问道。另一名军官回答：“没有。”

contentParagraphs.en: Their fears proved justified. A short time after being discharged, Descamps would be dead of an overdose from street drugs already in his system. A spokesman for Providence Milwaukie Hospital declined NPR's repeated requests for an interview about Descamps' case and didn't respond to detailed questions about his treatment.
contentParagraphs.zh: 事实证明，他们的担心是有道理的。出院后不久，德坎普斯就因体内已有的街头毒品过量而死亡。普罗维登斯密尔沃基医院的发言人拒绝了美国公共广播电台多次提出的有关德坎普斯案件的采访请求，也没有回答有关他的治疗的详细问题。

contentParagraphs.en: In a statement issued to the media after Descamps' death, the hospital expressed regret and acknowledged the care he received was inadequate. "In this case, we fell short of our goal of providing safe, reliable, compassionate care to our patient," it said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在德坎普去世后向媒体发表的一份声明中，医院表示遗憾，并承认他接受的护理不充分。 “在这种情况下，我们没有达到为患者提供安全、可靠、富有同情心的护理的目标，”它说。

contentParagraphs.en: But in interviews with more than a dozen doctors, scientists, federal officials and addiction activists, along with a review of research and government data, NPR found that what happened that night in Oregon is part of a troubling national pattern.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但在对十几位医生、科学家、联邦官员和毒瘾活动人士的采访以及对研究和政府数据的审查后，美国公共广播电台发现俄勒冈州那天晚上发生的事情是令人不安的全国模式的一部分。

contentParagraphs.en: People with serious alcohol or drug addiction in the U.S. regularly go to doctor's offices, clinics and hospitals, only to leave after receiving insufficient or no treatment, often with devastating consequences.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在美国，严重酗酒或吸毒的人经常去医生办公室、诊所和医院，但在治疗不足或没有治疗后就离开，这往往会带来毁灭性的后果。

contentParagraphs.en: "I think we should be outraged every single time someone dies from any condition that has treatment available that someone isn't getting," said Dr. Judy Chertok, who treats addiction patients and teaches medicine at the University of Pennsylvania. "We would not allow, as a society, people with heart attacks to come to a hospital and not get appropriate treatment. This is as serious as that."
contentParagraphs.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学治疗成瘾患者并教授医学的朱迪·切尔托克博士说：“我认为，每当有人因某种无法得到治疗的疾病而死亡时，我们都应该感到愤怒。” “作为一个社会，我们不会允许心脏病发作的人来到医院却得不到适当的治疗。这件事就这么严重。”

contentParagraphs.en: Most addiction patients get little or no treatment
contentParagraphs.zh: 大多数成瘾患者很少或根本没有得到治疗

contentParagraphs.en: Chertok is among the growing number of critics who say efforts to bring addiction treatment into the mainstream of American medicine have fallen short.
contentParagraphs.zh: 越来越多的批评者表示，将成瘾治疗纳入美国医学主流的努力尚未成功，切尔托克就是其中之一。

contentParagraphs.en: Addiction is widespread in the U.S., affecting more than 40 million people, according to the latest federal data released last month. While drug overdose deaths have dropped in recent years, alcohol- and drug-related disorders still kill more than 250,000 people every year. Meanwhile, research shows alcohol-related deaths have doubled over the last 20 years, while nonfatal overdoses from fentanyl are rising.
contentParagraphs.zh: 根据上个月发布的最新联邦数据，成瘾现象在美国很普遍，影响超过 4000 万人。尽管近年来吸毒过量死亡人数有所下降，但每年仍有超过 25 万人死于酒精和毒品相关疾病。与此同时，研究表明，过去 20 年来，与酒精相关的死亡人数增加了一倍，而芬太尼的非致命过量服用也在增加。

contentParagraphs.en: Despite that toll, the federal data released last month shows that in 2025 more than 80% of people who need help get no medical treatment of any kind for their addiction.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管如此，上个月发布的联邦数据显示，到 2025 年，超过 80% 需要帮助的人无法因毒瘾而得到任何形式的治疗。

contentParagraphs.en: "Much of what I do is scream back at that," Chertok told NPR. "Many who ultimately die from their [addiction-related] illness have had significant contacts with healthcare and social services agencies in the few months leading up to their deaths."
contentParagraphs.zh: 切尔托克告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“我所做的大部分事情都是对此尖叫回应。” “许多最终死于[成瘾相关]疾病的人在死亡前的几个月内与医疗保健和社会服务机构有过密切接触。”

contentParagraphs.en: In the case of Jean Descamps on that winter night in Oregon, death came much faster, after Milwaukie police decided to transport him to an emergency behavioral health center in nearby Portland.
contentParagraphs.zh: 俄勒冈州那个冬夜的让·德坎普斯（Jean Descamps）的案例中，密尔沃基警方决定将他送往波特兰附近的一个紧急行为健康中心后，他的死亡来得更快了。

contentParagraphs.en: On the body camera recording, officers can be heard growing increasingly alarmed by his condition as he sat in the back of a police cruiser. "Hey Jean, hey Jean!" one officer shouted, after searching for signs Descamps was breathing. "Boy, I don't know. Look at his eyes, I don't know."
contentParagraphs.zh: 从随身摄像机的录音中可以听到，当他坐在警车后座上时，警察对他的状况越来越感到震惊。 “嘿，简，嘿，简！”一名警官在寻找德坎普斯的呼吸迹象后喊道。 “小子，我不知道。看看他的眼睛，我不知道。”

contentParagraphs.en: In bodycam footage released by the Milwaukie Police Department, Descamps is seen in the hospital parking lot, unresponsive to surrounding officers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在密尔沃基警察局发布的随身摄像机镜头中，可以看到德坎普斯在医院停车场，对周围的警察没有反应。

contentParagraphs.en: Milwaukie Police Department/Screenshot by NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: 密尔沃基警察局/NPR 截图

articles.title: Cashing in on SpaceX: 'Every chance I get, I'll sell a little more'
articles.summary: Andre Lavoie joined SpaceX in 2009 as an engineer, now he's looking to cash in his shares in the company.
articles.titleZh: 从 SpaceX 获利：“一有机会，我就会多卖一点”
articles.summaryZh: 安德烈·拉沃伊 (Andre Lavoie) 于 2009 年加入 SpaceX，担任工程师，现在他希望将自己在该公司的股份变现。

contentParagraphs.en: Andre Lavoie joined SpaceX in 2009 as an engineer, designing the pressure tanks that help power its rocket. He was paid partly in stock - a common trade-off at start-ups as a hiring incentive.Some 17 years on, those 200,000 shares he was given are worth about $23m (£17m) - and the 63-year-old says he's ready to start cashing them as soon as he can."Every chance I get going forward, I'll sell a little bit more," he tells the BBC. "The shares have been going up so radically it keeps messing up my life plans - you really can't know the future, so it's better to sell early and in intervals."Lavoie is far from being the only one who has seen the value of his stake in SpaceX rocket over the years. The company's founder, Elon Musk, said on Fox News that SpaceX's listing on the stock market in June had likely made "several thousand" employees millionaires - including staff "who were working on the production line".According to reports, there are estimated to be 4,400 new millionaires created by the listing.Unlike most newly-listed firms, SpaceX shares are set to be released in stages: the first 20% on 6 August, with more due in batches through the rest of the year.Whether or not shareholders decide to sell their stake at the first opportunity is a matter for individuals. Unlike Lavoie, some may choose to hold onto their shares altogether in the hope of bigger gains later.SpaceX listed on the Nasdaq in June, in the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history, valuing the rocket and satellite firm at more than $2 trillion. It briefly made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire, before the stock cooled and his fortune slipped back below the milestone within weeks.In its first results as a public company this week, the firm's quarterly revenue was shown to have nearly doubled to $7.8bn (£5.8bn) from a year earlier, while its spending ballooned to $18.3bn - more than six times what it was a year ago.Overall, SpaceX made a net loss of $143m in the three months to June, and a loss of $2bn during the first six months of the year.Musk pushed back against sceptics on an earnings call: "I think people are really underestimating Starlink". He predicted the satellite internet service - the one part of the company that is currently making a profit - could one day deliver a majority of the world's internet.But shares in the company tumbled on the back of the earnings report, with investors generally spooked by the huge amounts of money being spent on AI.SpaceX shares fell 13.6% on Wednesday to $108.27 (£80.44) - well below the initial listing price of $135 a share.Lavoie plans to use his money from selling some of his shares to fund a hotel he is renovating in Pontebba, Italy's northeastern Friuli region, plus a small brewery.He says is priority for the future is raising awareness of air pollution in the area, in partnership with a local environmental group.Before he was hired, Lavoie was interviewed by Musk himself. "He's a very charming person when he wants something," Lavoie says. He wouldn't be drawn on Musk's politics - "that's his business" - but is unreserved about the company: "I've always been happily supportive and impressed, and would work hard with those incredible people again."Some analysts value SpaceX at less than half its current stock market price, warning its ties to xAI carry real financial risk - part of a broader worry on Wall Street that sky-high valuations for AI-linked firms, including SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic, could prove overdone.Sinead O'Sullivan, an economist who has previously worked for Nasa, told the BBC in June she thinks SpaceX is an "Elon Musk ego project"."You're buying a share of the Elon Musk brand more than any kind of space industry," she said.But Ron Epstein, an aerospace analyst at Bank of America Securities, says the recent share price swings say more about the market than the company. "A lot of it has to do with macro trends," he says. "None of it really has anything to do with what's going on fundamentally at the company."He says investors judging SpaceX purely as an AI bet are missing the point: "They're not just a compute provider. They're not just an AI company. It's a far more complicated picture than that."SpaceX, he adds, has cut the cost of reaching orbit from around $10,000-$20,000 a kilogram to about $2,000 with its Falcon 9 rocket - "they have built a railroad to space."Lavoie, for his part, isn't rattled. He says: "The solid business model of SpaceX will prove itself to be worth the investment,"even as he takes some of his own winnings off the table.
contentParagraphs.zh: 安德烈·拉沃伊 (Andre Lavoie) 于 2009 年加入 SpaceX，担任工程师，负责设计为其火箭提供动力的压力罐。他的部分薪酬是股票——这是初创企业作为招聘激励措施的常见做法。大约 17 年过去了，他获得的 20 万股股票价值约为 2300 万美元（1700 万英镑）——这位 63 岁的老人表示，他已经准备好尽快开始兑现这些股票。“每次有机会，我都会多卖一点，”他告诉 BBC。 “股价上涨如此之快，一直打乱了我的人生计划——你真的无法知道未来，所以最好尽早、间歇性地出售。”拉沃伊并不是多年来唯一一个看到自己所持 SpaceX 火箭股份价值的人。该公司创始人埃隆·马斯克在福克斯新闻上表示，SpaceX 6 月份在股市上市可能让“数千名”员工成为百万富翁，其中包括“在生产线上工作的员工”。据报道，此次上市预计将创造 4,400 名新百万富翁。与大多数新上市公司不同，SpaceX 股票将分阶段发行：首批 20% 于 8 月 6 日发行，更多股票将在 8 月 6 日分批发行。股东是否决定在第一时间出售其股份是个人的事情。与 Lavoie 不同的是，有些人可能会选择完全持有自己的股票，希望以后能获得更大的收益。 SpaceX 于 6 月在纳斯达克上市，这是历史上规模最大的首次公开募股 (IPO)，这家火箭和卫星公司的估值超过 2 万亿美元。这短暂地让埃隆·马斯克成为世界上第一位万亿富翁，但随后股价降温，他的财富在几周内回落到了这一里程碑以下。本周作为上市公司发布的首份业绩显示，该公司的季度收入较上年同期几乎翻了一番，达到 78 亿美元（合 58 亿英镑），而其支出则飙升至 183 亿美元，是一年前的六倍多。总体而言，SpaceX 在 2019 年的三个月内净亏损 1.43 亿美元。 6 月，今年前 6 个月亏损 20 亿美元。马斯克在财报电话会议上反驳了怀疑论者：“我认为人们真的低估了 Starlink”。他预测卫星互联网服务（该公司目前正在盈利的部分）有一天可能会提供全球大部分互联网服务。但该公司股价在财报发布后暴跌，投资者普遍对人工智能上投入的巨额资金感到惊慌。周三，SpaceX 股价下跌 13.6%，至 108.27 美元（80.44 英镑），远低于每股 135 美元的初始上市价格。拉沃伊计划用他的钱他出售部分股份，为他正在意大利东北部弗留利地区庞特巴翻修的一家酒店以及一家小啤酒厂提供资金。他表示，未来的首要任务是与当地环保组织合作，提高该地区对空气污染的认识。在受聘之前，拉沃伊接受了马斯克本人的采访。 “当他想要某样东西时，他是一个非常有魅力的人，”拉沃伊说。他不会受到马斯克的政治影响——“那是他的事”——但对这家公司毫无保留：“我一直很高兴地支持并印象深刻，并且会再次与这些令人难以置信的人一起努力工作。”一些分析师对 SpaceX 的估值不到当前股价的一半，警告其与 xAI 的关系存在真正的财务风险 - 华尔街普遍担心的一部分，即包括 SpaceX、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 在内的人工智能相关公司的天价估值可能会证明这一点过分了。曾在美国宇航局工作过的经济学家西尼德·奥沙利文 (Sinead O'Sullivan) 6 月份告诉 BBC，她认为 SpaceX 是一个“埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的自我项目”。“你购买埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 品牌的股份比购买任何类型的航天工业都多，”她说。但美国银行证券 (Bank of America Securities) 航空航天分析师罗恩·爱泼斯坦 (Ron Epstein) 表示，最近的股价波动更多地反映了市场而不是公司。 “这在很大程度上与宏观趋势有关，”他说。 “这一切都与公司的基本面没有任何关系。”他表示，纯粹将 SpaceX 视为人工智能赌注的投资者没有抓住要点：“他们不仅仅是一家计算提供商。他们不仅仅是一家人工智能公司。情况比这要复杂得多。”他补充道，SpaceX 已经通过猎鹰火箭将进入轨道的成本从每公斤 10,000 至 20,000 美元左右降低到了 2,000 美元左右。 9 号火箭——“他们建造了一条通往太空的铁路。” 拉沃伊则并不惊慌。他表示：“SpaceX 可靠的商业模式将证明自己值得投资，”尽管他自己也拿走了一些奖金。

articles.title: Meta becomes latest firm to say its AI hacked another company
articles.summary: Meta is the latest company to disclose an AI agent breach, raising cyber-security concerns.
articles.titleZh: Meta 成为最新一家称其人工智能攻击了另一家公司的公司
articles.summaryZh: Meta 是最新一家披露人工智能代理漏洞的公司，引发了网络安全担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: Facebook owner Meta has become the latest tech firm to say one of its AI models was able to connect to the internet and hack into another organisation's systems, during testing.The incident, which Meta says occurred during an evaluation by an independent company, is the fourth recent incident of its kind disclosed by AI companies.Similar breaches by OpenAI and Anthropic models have raised cyber-security concerns and prompted calls for tougher safeguards and more rigorous testing.A Meta spokesperson told the BBC that it was investigating the hack, which it said had been caused by a "misconfiguration" by its independent tester.It also described what happened as similar to previously reported incidents at other firms.Meta said the security trials were conducted by Irregular, the same AI security vendor that carried out tests for Anthropic's AI model that had gained access to three other companies' systems.An Irregular spokesperson said the Meta incident "is the exact same evaluation-environment issue that was already disclosed by Anthropic last week."Irregular is working on a report on how to securely run cyber-security tests involving AI agents, the firm's spokesperson told the BBC.Meta also said it will publish more information on the incident "once we have all the facts."In the past two weeks, AI leaders OpenAI and Anthropic have also reported incidents in which their models hacked into other organisation's systems during testing.ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said in a series of announcements that its agents attacked several publicly available services, including AI tools hub Hugging Face.OpenAI's disclosure prompted rival Anthropic to conduct its own checks, leading to the discovery that its Claude AI model had carried out similar attacks on several firms after a "misconfiguration" gave it access to the internet. Daniel Hulme, global chief AI officer of advertising firm WPP, told the BBC that such AI models "are not conscious — they're not deliberately doing something devious"."What they're doing is coming up with very sophisticated strategies or cyberattacks to be able to achieve the goal that they've been given," he told the Today programme."When you give an AI a goal, if you don't think of all the ways it might be able to achieve the goal, it will find a way to achieve a goal that you haven't thought about."
contentParagraphs.zh: Facebook 所有者 Meta 成为最新一家表示其人工智能模型能够在测试过程中连接到互联网并侵入另一个组织系统的科技公司。Meta 表示，这一事件是在一家独立公司的评估过程中发生的，这是人工智能公司最近披露的第四起此类事件。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 模型的类似违规行为引发了网络安全担忧，并促使人们呼吁采取更严格的保障措施和更严格的测试。Meta 发言人告诉 BBC，它正在调查这起黑客事件，据称这是由它也描述了所发生的情况与之前报告的其他公司的事件类似。Meta 表示，安全试验是由 Irregular 进行的，Irregular 是对 Anthropic 的 AI 模型进行测试的同一家 AI 安全供应商，该模型已获得对其他三家公司系统的访问权限。Irregular 发言人表示，Meta 事件“与 Anthropic 上周已经披露的评估环境问题完全相同。”Irregular 正在编写一份关于如何安全运行涉及以下内容的网络安全测试的报告：该公司发言人告诉 BBC。Meta 还表示，“一旦我们掌握了所有事实”，它将发布有关该事件的更多信息。过去两周，人工智能领导者 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 也报告了他们的模型在测试过程中入侵其他组织系统的事件。ChatGPT 制造商 OpenAI 在一系列公告中表示，其代理攻击了多项公开服务，包括人工智能工具中心 Hugging Face。OpenAI 的披露促使竞争对手 Anthropic 进行了自己的检查，导致发现其 Claude AI 模型在“错误配置”使其能够访问互联网后，对几家公司进行了类似的攻击。广告公司 WPP 全球首席人工智能官丹尼尔·休姆 (Daniel Hulme) 告诉 BBC，此类人工智能模型“没有意识——它们不会故意做一些不正当的事情”。他在《今日》节目中表示，“它们所做的是想出非常复杂的策略或网络攻击，以实现既定的目标。”你还没有想过。”

articles.title: Majority of England's rivers and lakes fail new environmental review
articles.summary: A comprehensive assessment of England's waterways is the first in six years and shows little improvement.
articles.titleZh: 英格兰大部分河流和湖泊未能通过新的环境审查
articles.summaryZh: 这是六年来首次对英格兰水道进行全面评估，但进展甚微。

contentParagraphs.en: The government is already on course to miss its legally binding target of restoring 77% of England's waters to good ecological status by 2027 - a goal the environmental watchdog, the Office for Environmental Protection, has warned will be missed by a "considerable margin".It's now investigating both the government and the Environment Agency over possible rule breaches.Environment Secretary Angela Eagle said the figures "underline the need for wholesale change across the water sector".She pointed to new laws the government has introduced to hold water companies to account and record investment. "We will drive forward a system that puts the public interest first," she said.Much of the debate about the state of England's waters has centred on water companies and the sewage they release into rivers. But campaigners and scientists also point to agriculture as an equally large source of pollution - one that attracts far less public attention.Erica Popplewell, of the campaign group River Action, said some farming, particularly intensive poultry units - vast sheds housing hundreds of thousands of birds - were a growing threat to rivers such as the Wye and Severn."There's a lot of poo that comes out of the chickens," she said. "If it goes straight into a river, it causes eutrophication. The whole ecology of the river is damaged, and the river is dying." She called on the government to tackle sewage and farming "with the same urgency".The National Farmers' Union of England and Wales has been approached for comment.Other types of pollution affecting England's bodies of water, the Environment Agency pointed to, include petrol, garden pesticides and contaminated water running off roads picking up microplastics.The Environment Agency stressed that this year's data could not be directly compared with 2019 because it had changed its methods.In particular, it said the steep fall in the number of lakes ranked as good - down about half from 2019 - largely reflected a change in how its experts now assess them, rather than a genuine decline in their condition.Its chair, Alan Lovell, acknowledged too many water bodies were "still not achieving the standards we want to see", adding that the agency was "transforming our enforcement work" with its largest ever workforce.But Prof Penny Johnes, a leading water quality scientist at the University of Bristol, told BBC News the true picture was almost certainly worse than the classifications suggested.The scheme was "not fit for purpose", she said, measuring too few pollutants too infrequently, and missing nitrogen and other substances scientists have long understood to be driving rivers' decline.The findings come as much of England sits in official drought, with rivers running low and more than 20 million people facing hosepipe bans. Lower flows can concentrate the very pollution the new data is designed to track, leaving fish and other aquatic life exposed to more dangerous levels. Hundreds of dead fish linked to heatwave and pollutionClimate change is expected to bring drier and hotter summers which could further exacerbate this issue. Asked directly whether England's waters were healthier than six or seven years ago, Prof Johnes said: "No, definitely not."Every river and lake failed the test for chemical pollution.The Environment Agency said this is because legacy substances, such as heavy metals from mining, take decades to break down, and some are building up. But Prof Johnes said it was also a "failure to regulate effectively" the new chemicals entering rivers, from antibiotics to the "forever chemicals" known as PFAS - many not routinely monitored.There are currently 23 enforcement notices against water companies requiring them to lower the levels of PFAS to reduce the danger to human health.Water UK, which represents the water companies, has called for PFAS use to be banned to limit their build-up and reduce water treatment costs, but the chemicals are currently used in thousands of products, from school uniforms to medical devices.It said it was spending record amounts of money on improving the country's waterways."Water companies are investing £22bn in environmental improvements by 2030. This will help to secure our water supplies, support economic growth and end sewage entering our rivers and seas."The Environment Agency also noted that other European countries are doing even worse in terms of the good health of their waterways, with only 8% in Germany and just 1% in the Netherlands.But Prof Johnes said such a comparison is misleading, because of varying methodologies across nations.

articles.title: Indian journalist Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years in jail for rape
articles.summary: Tejpal, who has denied the accusations, can appeal against the verdict in India's Supreme Court.
articles.titleZh: 印度记者塔伦·泰帕尔因强奸罪被判入狱10年
articles.summaryZh: 泰杰帕尔否认了这些指控，他可以就印度最高法院的判决提出上诉。

contentParagraphs.en: An Indian court has sentenced former Tehelka magazine editor Tarun Tejpal to 10 years in prison for raping a former colleague, overturning his 2021 acquittal in a decade-old case.The Goa bench of the Bombay High Court convicted Tejpal under sections of Indian law pertaining to rape and sexual harassment.Along with jail terms which run concurrently, the court has also ordered him to pay fines adding up to more than 1mn rupees ($10,500; £7,800).Tejpal, who has denied the accusations, said before the sentencing that he would file an appeal in the Supreme Court.The allegations against Tejpal, one of India's best-known editors, had made national headlines in 2013. A year before that, thousands of Indians had participated in protests after a brutal gang rape and murder of a woman in Delhi, leading to a larger conversation on sexual violence.Tejpal's accuser, who cannot be identified under Indian law, said that he sexually assaulted her in a lift during Tehelka's high-profile international conference in Goa in November 2013, an event attended by, among others, Hollywood star Robert De Niro. Judge questions 'appropriate' behaviour for rape victimsTarun Tejpal: Powerful and pioneering journalistTejpal initially blamed the assault on "a lapse of judgement" and "a misreading of the situation" which had "led to an unfortunate incident that rails against all we believe in and fight for".But as the case escalated, he issued a statement urging authorities to examine the CCTV footage "so the accurate version of events stands clearly revealed". He also alleged that the case against him was part of a "political vendetta" by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Goa.Tehelka, the magazine Tejpal co-founded in 2000, had published a number of scoops, many of them based on sting operations.Some of these stories - including Operation West End in which some of its journalists posed as arms dealers, secretly filming senior army officials, bureaucrats and even the president of the then ruling BJP taking bribes to push through a fake deal - created national and international ripples.Tejpal was arrested in 2013 and spent seven months in jail until the Supreme Court granted him bail.In 2021, a sessions court in Goa threw out all the charges against him. But the judge's observations in the 527-page order sparked criticism after she questioned the behaviour of the survivor..In photographs taken shortly after the assault, the judge wrote, the young woman was "smiling and looked happy, normal, in [a] good mood"."She did not look disturbed, reserved, terrified or traumatised in any way even though this was immediately after she claims to have been sexually assaulted," the order said. The Goa government had appealed against the acquittal in the high court. Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had urged the high court to impose the maximum sentence on Tejpal."This court must give a clear message to society that when a girl says no, it means no," Livelaw quoted him as saying."All I can say is I am 62. I believe I am a political victim. I am a father of two daughters. I have a wife. All we can say is we will go up and appeal. My lawyer wants me to request you to be lenient," legal website Bar and Bench quoted Tejpal as telling the court before the sentencing.Tejpal was found guilty under legal sections including 376(2)(f), which pertains to rape committed by "a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman".
contentParagraphs.zh: 印度一家法院因强奸前同事而判处 Tehelka 杂志前编辑 Tarun Tejpal 10 年监禁，推翻了 2021 年对这起十年前案件的无罪判决。孟买高等法院果阿法官根据印度法律有关强奸和性骚扰的条款判定 Tejpal 有罪。除了同时执行的监禁外，法院还命令他支付总计超过 100 万美元的罚款。卢比（10,500 美元；7,800 英镑）。泰杰帕尔否认了这些指控，他在宣判前表示，他将向最高法院提出上诉。针对印度最著名编辑之一的泰杰帕尔的指控曾在 2013 年成为全国头条新闻。一年前，一名妇女在德里遭到残酷轮奸和谋杀，数千名印度人参加了抗议活动，引发了一场关于性问题的更大讨论。根据印度法律，泰杰帕尔的原告身份无法公开。他表示，2013 年 11 月，特赫尔卡在果阿举行备受瞩目的国际会议期间，他在电梯里对她进行了性侵犯，好莱坞明星罗伯特·德尼罗 (Robert De Niro) 等人也出席了这次活动。法官质疑强奸受害者的“适当”行为塔伦·泰帕尔：强大而先锋的记者泰帕尔最初将这次袭击归咎于“判断失误”和“对形势的误读”，“导致了一场不幸的事件，违背了我们所信仰和为之奋斗的一切”。但随着案件升级，他发表声明，敦促当局检查闭路电视录像，“以便清楚地揭示事件的准确版本”。他还声称，针对他的案件是果阿印度人民党 (BJP) 政府“政治仇杀”的一部分。 Tejpal 于 2000 年与他人共同创办的杂志《Tehelka》发表了许多独家新闻，其中许多是基于诱骗行动。然后裁定印度人民党收受贿赂以推动一项虚假交易，在国内和国际上引起了轩然大波。Tejpal 于 2013 年被捕，并在监狱中度过了七个月，直到最高法院批准他保释。2021 年，果阿的一个法庭驳回了对他的所有指控。但法官在这份长达 527 页的命令中提出的意见，在她对幸存者的行为提出质疑后，引发了批评。法官写道，在袭击发生后不久拍摄的照片中，这名年轻女子“面带微笑，看起来很高兴、正常，心情很好”。命令称，“她看起来没有任何不安、矜持、害怕或创伤，尽管这是在她声称遭到性侵犯之后立即发生的。”果阿政府已就高等法院的无罪释放提出上诉。果阿政府副检察长图沙尔·梅赫塔 (Tushar Mehta) 代表果阿政府出庭，敦促高等法院对特杰帕尔处以最高刑罚。“这个法院必须向社会发出明确的信息，当一个女孩说‘不’时，那就意味着‘不’，”利夫劳援引他的话说。“我只能说，我今年 62 岁。我相信我是政治受害者。我是两个女儿的父亲。我有妻子。我们只能说我们会上去上诉。我的律师要我请求你法律网站Bar and Bench援引Tejpal在量刑前对法庭的说法。Tejpal根据包括第376(2)(f)条在内的法律条款被判有罪，该条款涉及“该妇女的亲戚、监护人或老师，或对该妇女有信任或权威的人”实施的强奸。

articles.title: Restaurants, pubs and theatres ban Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ over privacy fears
articles.summary:
Meta says safeguards are in place to prevent surreptitious filming, but some UK venues now prohibit them from being worn at all
When Meta used superstar Kylie Jenner to promote its sleek new line of “spy glasses”, the social media company hoped the devices would reach the same br
articles.titleZh: 出于隐私担忧，餐馆、酒吧和剧院禁止 Meta 的“间谍眼镜”
articles.summaryZh:
梅塔表示，已经采取了保护措施来防止秘密拍摄，但英国一些场所现在根本禁止佩戴它们
当 Meta 利用超级明星凯莉·詹纳 (Kylie Jenner) 来宣传其时尚的新系列“间谍眼镜”时，这家社交媒体公司希望这些设备能够达到同样的目标。

contentParagraphs.en: When Meta used superstar Kylie Jenner to promote its sleek new line of “spy glasses”, the social media company hoped the devices would reach the same broad acceptance that tablets and smartwatches have found before them.But those plans have hit a snag in the UK, where venues from elite restaurants to popular pub chains have banned the £359 glasses in order to preserve the privacy of customers and staff.Celebrated restaurateur Jeremy King, owner of London venues including Simpsons in the Strand, Arlington and The Park, said guests should not wear the recording glasses.He told the Guardian: “I would never knowingly allow any invasion of guest privacy other than with the eyes we were born with.”Restaurateur Jeremy King looks unfavourably on the smartglasses in his restaurants.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当 Meta 利用超级巨星凯莉·詹纳 (Kylie Jenner) 宣传其时尚的新系列“间谍眼镜”时，这家社交媒体公司希望这些设备能够像平板电脑和智能手表一样获得广泛接受。但这些计划在英国遇到了障碍，为了保护顾客和员工的隐私，从高级餐厅到受欢迎的酒吧连锁店都禁止使用价值 359 英镑的眼镜。公园表示，客人不应佩戴录音眼镜。他告诉《卫报》：“除了我们与生俱来的眼睛之外，我绝不会故意允许任何侵犯客人隐私的行为。” 餐厅老板杰里米·金 (Jeremy King) 对他餐厅中的智能眼镜持不满态度。

contentParagraphs.en: Photograph: Dave Benett/Getty Images for Christina MakrisThose wearing the glasses in Soho House’s private members’ clubs can also be expected to be asked to remove them. A spokesperson confirmed filming is not allowed in their venues, and these devices are no exception.Even pub chain Wetherspoons will not allow people to record using the glasses inside.Tim Martin, its chief executive, said: “The general code that applies in our pubs, and most pubs, is that you can’t film customers or employees without their permission. Meta glasses seem to breach this code, and common sense, by enabling surreptitious surveillance, so our instinct is to say turn off the cameras. This is akin to our efforts to stop audible playing of videos in our pubs, which also invades people’s space.”Those who want to wear their Meta glasses to the theatre may face obstacles too. A spokesperson for ATG Theatres, which owns the Bristol Hippodrome, Edinburgh Playhouse, and various theatres across London, said that filming is not allowed and that those wearing the glasses during shows will be asked to remove them.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionThe glasses resemble normal eyewear, with the Jenner-designed model featuring a fashionable cat-eye design – with tiny cameras embedded. Meta says it hopes that the design allows users to stay “in the moment” without constantly looking down at a smartphone.There have been widespread fears about the glasses being used to film people without their consent, with the resultant footage posted on social media. Though Meta points to the tiny, flashing LED light that activates on the glasses when they are being used to film, there have already been multiple instances of people complaining they have been videoed without prior knowledge.In one instance, a woman told the BBC a man recorded her, and then demanded money to remove the videos from social media. Another woman described being recorded during sexual encounters without her consent.Instagram has cracked down on nonconsensual videos made using the glasses posted on the platform. “If you’re posting content that is taking advantage of people and harassing them, like a lot of these pickup line kind of videos that we’ve heard of and seen, then we’re going to take the content down,” Instagram head Adam Mosseri said.Guardian journalist Elle Hunt put Meta’s smartglasses through its paces on the streets of Norwich earlier this year. Photograph: Ali Smith/The GuardianMeta has tried hard to make wearing the glasses a mainstream choice, handing out free pairs to popular social media influencers. Sales of the devices have tripled in the last year, with more than 7m sold worldwide.Those seven million people do have some venues in the UK where they and their glasses are welcome. Michelin starred chef Tom Kerridge, who owns pubs and restaurants in Marlow, told the Guardian: “I have no problem whatsoever with them. Filming is part of everyday life now. In fact I think that they can be used in creative and exciting ways. The first thought about them shouldn’t be negative!”A Meta spokesperson said: “People use our glasses because they’re genuinely helpful – from listening to music, to live translation or hands-free calls. For those wearing them and the people around them, trust matters. That’s why we built privacy into our AI glasses from the ground up. For example, every pair has a capture LED that blinks when you take a photo or video that you can save or share, it can’t be turned off, and if someone covers or damages the LED, the camera is disabled.”
contentParagraphs.zh: 照片：Dave Benett/Getty Images for Christina Makris 那些在 Soho House 私人会员俱乐部戴眼镜的人也可能会被要求摘下眼镜。一位发言人证实，他们的场地内不允许拍摄，这些设备也不例外。即使是连锁酒吧 Wetherspoons 也不允许人们使用里面的眼镜进行录音。其首席执行官蒂姆·马丁 (Tim Martin) 表示：“适用于我们酒吧和大多数酒吧的通用守则是，未经顾客或员工许可，不得拍摄顾客或员工。Meta 眼镜似乎违反了这一守则和常识，因为它可以进行秘密监视，所以我们的本能是关掉摄像头。这就像我们努力阻止酒吧里的视频有声播放一样，这也侵犯了人们的空间。”那些想戴 Meta 眼镜去剧院的人也可能面临障碍。拥有布里斯托尔赛马场、爱丁堡剧院和伦敦各地多家剧院的 ATG 剧院的发言人表示，不允许拍摄，并且在演出期间佩戴眼镜的人将被要求摘下眼镜。 这种眼镜类似于普通眼镜，詹纳设计的型号采用时尚的猫眼设计，并嵌入微型相机。 Meta 表示，它希望这种设计能让用户“活在当下”，而不必一直低头看智能手机。人们普遍担心这款眼镜会在未经他人同意的情况下对人们进行拍摄，并将拍摄的视频发布在社交媒体上。尽管 Meta 指出，眼镜上的微小闪烁 LED 灯在用于拍摄时会激活，但已经有多起人们抱怨自己在事先不知情的情况下被录像的情况。 在一个案例中，一名女子告诉 BBC 一名男子录下了她的视频，然后索要钱财将这些视频从社交媒体上删除。另一名女性称，在未经她同意的情况下，性行为过程中被录像。Instagram 已严厉打击使用该平台上发布的眼镜制作的未经同意的视频。 Instagram 负责人亚当·莫塞里 (Adam Mosseri) 表示：“如果你发布的内容利用他人并骚扰他们，比如我们听说过、看过的许多搭讪视频，那么我们就会删除这些内容。” 今年早些时候，《卫报》记者艾丽·亨特 (Elle Hunt) 在诺维奇的街道上测试了 Meta 的智能眼镜。照片：Ali Smith/The GuardianMeta 努力让佩戴眼镜成为主流选择，向受欢迎的社交媒体影响者免费赠送一副眼镜。去年，这些设备的销量增加了两倍，全球销量超过 700 万台。在英国确实有一些场所欢迎他们和他们的眼镜。在马洛拥有酒吧和餐馆的米其林星级厨师汤姆·克里奇 (Tom Kerridge) 告诉《卫报》：“我对它们没有任何问题。拍摄现在已成为日常生活的一部分。事实上，我认为它们可以以创造性和令人兴奋的方式使用。对它们的第一反应不应该是负面的！”Meta 发言人表示：“人们使用我们的眼镜是因为它们确实很有帮助——从听音乐到现场翻译或免提通话。对于佩戴它们的人和周围的人来说，请相信它们这就是为什么我们从头开始将隐私融入到 AI 眼镜中，例如，每副眼镜都有一个拍摄 LED，当您拍摄可以保存或分享的照片或视频时，它会闪烁，并且如果有人遮盖或损坏 LED，相机就会被禁用。”

articles.title: Shorts, strappy tops and sandals: What is acceptable to wear in the office?
articles.summary: Here's how to style for success while keeping your cool - and where you and your boss stand on your wardrobe.
articles.titleZh: 短裤、系带上衣和凉鞋：在办公室可以穿什么？

contentParagraphs.en: Shorts, strappy tops and sandals: What is acceptable to wear in the office?Image source, Getty ImagesByYasmin RufoBusiness reporter Yet another summer heatwave could be on the way to make your commute sweaty and your workplace stuffy.What to wear to work in the summer can be a surprisingly difficult decision. Shorts, strappy tops and sandals may keep you cool - but will they be judged too casual, revealing or unprofessional?There's a bare-legged backlash in Tokyo where officials encouraged men to swap suits for shorts at work, prompting complaints about hairy legs in the office.So what is acceptable to wear to work, how can you successfully style your summer wardrobe and can your boss tell you what you can and can't wear?Figure caption, Should men be allowed to wear shorts in the office?Conor, who works in media, has regularly worn shorts to the office during the recent hot weather. "Who gives a monkey's what you wear?" he says. "If you're able to do your job safely, professionally and appropriately, there's a lot to be said for letting people be comfortable."And many seem to agree - a recent poll by market research firm Ipsos found 62% of adults thought it was acceptable for men to wear shorts to work in hot weather, while 63% said the same for women.But we aren't talking short-shorts or denim hot pants fashion designer Amanda Wakeley points out: "If you're asking yourself whether they're too short, they probably are".She says shorts are "the trickiest item to get right in a professional environment" and recommends tailored, longer shorts paired with a crisp shirt or lightweight blazer for both men and women.Stylist Clare Chambers agrees shorts should sit around the kneecap for both men and women. For men, she recommends tailored chino-style shorts with an untucked T-shirt or shirt.Sandals Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Socks and sandals are a combo hard to pull off at the best of times, let alone in the officeWakeley describes flip-flops as one of the few definite "no" items in most offices. "They instantly signal leisure rather than professionalism and can make even the most polished outfit feel underdressed," she says.Chambers agrees, and says even during the hottest weather, woven flats are a better option because they are breathable while still covering the foot.Almost two-thirds of people questioned by Ipsos said they were unacceptable for men in the workplace, while 58% said the same for women.Sandals, however, are a slightly different matter as Wakeley says refined leather sandals can be entirely acceptable in many offices, provided they are clean and well maintained.The difference, she says, is whether they look like part of a considered outfit or something that would normally be worn around a swimming pool.She adds that while socks and sandals have become a viral fashion trend "it's important to consider whether a trend aligns with the image you want to communicate professionally". "This combination can read as highly casual and youthful, which may unintentionally detract from giving you a credible and authoritative presence."Strappy topsImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Public opinion is divided over bare shoulders at workSome 40% of adults considered tank tops or vest tops acceptable for women at work, compared with only 24% who said the same for men, according to Ipsos.Natasia, a teacher in London, says at a previous school she and other staff had been summoned "regularly in the summer months to tell us off about our outfits."She says she was also told to cover up her tattoos. "It should be OK to have your arms out at work especially when it's hot," she says.Wakeley says a well-cut camisole or strappy top can work when worn beneath a linen overshirt, lightweight jacket or tailored co-ord. On its own, however, it may feel too informal.Chambers says if you're wearing a strappy top "you must wear a strapless bra as it utterly kills an outfit when you can see bra straps".She explains that thicker straps are a safer option where the dress code is unclear and recommends satin camisoles as a more polished alternative to basic cotton vests.She adds that while bandeau tops are "such an on-trend look this summer, they are a no-go for work"."The constant need to keep fiddling to pull them up displays an uncomfortable and unconfident demeanour," she says.How to style summer clothes at workImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The answer to dressing for the heat isn't necessarily to wear less, but to choose clothes more carefullyWakeley and Chambers both say that you don't need to lose your personal style when dressing for the office and you can still inject plenty of personality while following a dress code. Here are their top tips on how to style summer clothes for the office. Can your employer tell you what to wear?Climate change is expected to bring more severe, frequent and longer-lasting heatwaves in UK summers in the coming years.Employers are allowed to set standards around clothing and appearance, particularly where there are legitimate reasons such as safety, branding or maintaining a professional image.But employment lawyer Sarah Tahamtani says dress codes should be "reasonable, proportionate and capable of justification"."During extreme heat, employers should consider whether existing requirements remain practical and whether greater flexibility can be introduced."They must also consider employees with disabilities, medical conditions or other vulnerabilities that may be worsened by high temperatures.An employee who believes a request is unreasonable or inconsistently applied should first raise the issue with a manager or HR and explain how the rule is affecting their comfort or ability to work safely.
contentParagraphs.zh: 短裤、系带上衣和凉鞋：在办公室穿什么是可以接受的？图片来源：Getty Images 作者：Yasmin Rufo Business 记者 另一场夏季热浪可能即将来临，让你的通勤路上出汗，让你的工作场所闷热。夏天穿什么去上班可能是一个非常困难的决定。短裤、系带上衣和凉鞋可能会让你保持凉爽，但它们会被认为过于休闲、暴露或不专业吗？在东京，人们强烈反对光腿，官员们鼓励男性在工作中把西装换成短裤，这引发了人们对办公室里腿部毛茸茸的抱怨。那么，穿什么上班可以接受，你如何才能成功地打造你的夏季衣柜，你的老板能告诉你什么可以穿，什么不可以穿吗？图标题，是否应该允许男性在办公室穿短裤办公室？在媒体工作的康纳在最近炎热的天气里经常穿着短裤去办公室。 “你穿的衣服是谁给猴子的？”他说。 “如果你能够安全、专业、恰当地完成你的工作，那么让人们感到舒适就有很多话可说。”许多人似乎都同意——市场研究公司益普索 (Ipsos) 最近的一项民意调查发现，62% 的成年人认为男性在炎热的天气里穿短裤上班是可以接受的，而 63% 的女性也这么认为。但我们说的不是短裤或牛仔热裤。时装设计师 Amanda Wakeley 指出：“如果你问自己是否她说短裤是“在职业环境中最难穿的单品”，并建议男性和女性都选择剪裁较长的短裤，搭配挺括的衬衫或轻便的西装外套。造型师克莱尔·钱伯斯（Clare Chambers）同意，无论男性还是女性，短裤都应位于膝盖骨周围。对于男士，她建议穿着剪裁合身的斜纹棉布短裤，搭配不塞进裤腰的 T 恤或衬衫。 凉鞋 图片来源，Getty Images 图片说明，即使在最好的时候，袜子和凉鞋也是很难搭配的组合，更不用说在办公室了。韦克利将人字拖描述为大多数办公室中少数明确“禁止”的物品之一。她说：“它们立刻就体现出休闲而不是专业精神，即使是最精致的服装也会给人一种朴素的感觉。”钱伯斯对此表示同意，并表示即使在最热的天气里，编织平底鞋也是更好的选择，因为它们透气，同时仍能遮住脚部。在益普索的受访者中，近三分之二的人表示，这种鞋对于职场男性来说是不可接受的，而 58% 的人也表示，对于女性来说也是如此。然而，凉鞋则略有不同，正如韦克利所说的精制皮革鞋一样。在许多办公室里，凉鞋是完全可以接受的，只要它们干净且保养得好。她说，区别在于它们是否看起来像是经过深思熟虑的服装的一部分，还是通常在游泳池周围穿着的东西。她补充说，虽然袜子和凉鞋已成为一种病毒式的时尚趋势，但“重要的是要考虑这种趋势是否与您想要专业沟通的形象相符”。 “这种组合读起来非常休闲和年轻，可能会无意中损害你的可信度和权威性。” 系带上衣 图片来源，盖蒂图片社 图片说明，工作中裸肩的公众舆论存在分歧 根据益普索的数据，大约 40% 的成年人认为女性在工作中穿背心或背心是可以接受的，而只有 24% 的人认为男性也可以接受同样的穿搭。她说，她“在夏季定期被叫来告诉我们服装的问题”。她说，她还被告知要遮盖纹身。她说：“工作时伸出双臂应该没什么问题，尤其是在天气炎热的时候。”韦克利说，剪裁考究的吊带背心或系带上衣可以穿在亚麻外套衬衫、轻便夹克或剪裁合身的衣服里面。然而，就其本身而言，可能会感觉太不正式。钱伯斯说，如果你穿着系带上衣，“你必须穿无肩带文胸，因为当你看到文胸肩带时，它完全毁了整套衣服”。她解释说，在着装要求不明确的情况下，较粗的肩带是一个更安全的选择，并建议缎面吊带背心作为基本棉背心的更精致的替代品。她补充说，虽然抹胸式上衣“是今年夏天的流行造型，但它们是不适合的”她说：“不断地摆弄衣服显示出一种不舒服和不自信的举止。”如何在工作中设计夏季服装图片来源，盖蒂图片社图片说明，在炎热的天气着装的答案不一定是穿得少，而是要更仔细地选择衣服韦克利和钱伯斯都表示，在办公室着装时不需要失去个人风格，在遵守着装规范的同时仍然可以注入足够的个性。以下是他们关于如何为办公室设计夏季服装的重要提示。你的雇主能告诉你穿什么吗？未来几年，气候变化预计将在英国夏季带来更严重、更频繁和更持久的热浪。雇主可以就着装和外表制定标准，特别是在有安全、品牌或维护专业形象等正当理由的情况下。但就业律师莎拉·塔哈姆塔尼表示，着装规范应该“合理、相称且能够证明其合理性”。他们还必须考虑残疾、健康状况或其他可能因高温而恶化的脆弱性的员工。如果员工认为要求不合理或不一致，应首先向经理或人力资源部门提出问题，并解释该规则如何影响他们的舒适度或安全工作的能力。

articles.title: Marmots facing money troubles turn to OnlyFans
articles.summary: A Colorado lab researching the ground-squirrels comes up with an innovative way to raise money after funding cuts.

contentParagraphs.en: Marmots - chubby, ground-dwelling squirrels - are the latest stars on the adult platform OnlyFans.That's thanks to the efforts of Colorado-based biologist Dr Daniel Blumstein, the head of a long-running field study on marmots, who was worried about its financial future after federal funding to universities was cut. Blumstein told the BBC he recently launched an account on OnlyFans, which is known mostly for sexually explicit content, and began posting "uncensored marmot content" in "an act of desperation". This content is family-friendly videos of the rodents scurrying around and popping out of their burrows, which so far has generated more than $5,000 (£3,712). After OnlyFans takes its share, the UCLA-affiliated Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Colorado will make about $4,000.The Marmot Project, which has been running for more than 60 years, is the second-longest study of individually identified mammals in the world, after Jane Goodall's chimpanzee study in Tanzania.It studies the yellow-bellied marmot, one of the 15 recognised species of marmot found in the Northern Hemisphere.Because the species is neither threatened nor endangered, it helps scientists to understand the factors that drive population changes, according to the lab. Blumstein said long-term studies such as these are really effective but, despite this, he has been unable to secure federal support. While the lab will probably not be able to generate enough money through OnlyFans to save the project from spending cuts, he believes raising awareness about their work is also important.The OnlyFans idea came to him when he sat in a meadow waiting for some marmots to pop out of the ground. Blumstein had recently watched the TV show Margot's Got Money Troubles, where Elle Fanning's character starts an OnlyFans account to support herself as a single mother."Marmots' got money troubles," he thought to himself. "Maybe we should do something a little risqué".He raised the idea with his lab students, and they came up with the name OnlyMarms. One student helped him set up the account.That's when he hit a slight snag. He had to upload a photo of his driver's licence to verify his identity. But the platform flagged that he did not look like the account's profile photo of a marmot. A quick email exchange cleared the way for them to start posting videos. On OnlyMarms, users can see the Rocky Mountain marmots in their natural habitat. They aren't as social as their alpine counterparts, Blumstein said, and the female marmots get grumpier as they age. In one video, a female marmot chases away a male who got too comfortable in her burrow. In another, a female is dubbed "the queen of the town" as she is caught on camera in the sun.The lab doesn't give their subjects human-sounding names, in an effort to avoid bias in their research. Instead, they mark the rodents with dye and call them things like "dans_hat", "open_kite" and "Citroën".The scientists have also launched Fat Marmot Week, styled after Fat Bear Week, where the public can vote for their favourite rotund rodent in a bracket-style tournament at the end of August. As hibernating animals, marmots put on weight before winter. "It's fun to root for the chunkiest marmot, but behind the fun and games is a deathly serious competition against nature to pile on fat to survive the long, cold winter," Blumstein said in a press release announcing the tournament.

contentParagraphs.en: The cosy relationship between Washington and Rabat has long been flaunted by both sides, from Morocco’s announcement this year that it would be the first African state to join Donald Trump’s Board of Peace to the congratulatory message recently sent by Trump to mark King Mohammed VI’s 27 years in power.The latest example landed this week. As Spain grappled with the aftermath of the sudden influx – and swift return – of more than 70,000 people into Ceuta, Morocco’s monarch confirmed he had named a $1bn highway flanking the disputed territory of Western Sahara after Trump.The deepening ties have come under renewed scrutiny as questions continue to swirl over what exactly led to the deadly mass border crossing into the tiny Spanish territory in north Africa.“I think there’s enough evidence to hypothesise or claim that Morocco is behind this,” said Riccardo Fabiani, the north Africa project director for the International Crisis Group. “But there was no clear trigger for this, and this is what is puzzling for everyone.”Migrants in Spain's Ceuta enclave escorted back to Morocco – videoObservers have suggested Spain’s recent rapprochement with Rabat’s archrival, Algeria, could have set off Morocco. But another, perhaps more plausible explanation pointed towards the US, said Fabiani.“It’s obviously impossible to demonstrate,” he said. “But in terms of plausibility, I don’t think it’s impossible to imagine that Morocco might have done something to earn brownie points with its allies, given that Morocco and this particular administration in Washington do have a very close, excellent relationship.”While Morocco had likely not “masterminded” the surge into Ceuta, he said, its relationship with the Trump administration – along with the Moroccan king’s desire to keep its claim to Ceuta in the spotlight – may have affected how it responded to fast-spreading online rumours about the Spanish border being thrown open.A young person is escorted by Spanish security forces after attempting to cross into Ceuta on Saturday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters“For sure the Moroccan security forces were monitoring those conversations,” said Fabiani. “They saw that and there was probably some conversation where they decided to do nothing and see where this goes.”What followed made headlines across the globe as tens of thousands of people swam or waded across one of the EU’s two land borders with Africa. As Spain scrambled to cope, far-right voices seized on the images.In the US, the vice-president, JD Vance, and the state department blamed the influx on the Socialist-led government of Spain, while Trump warned that electing Democrats would make what happened in Spain “look small-time”. At no point did any of them mention Morocco or the potential role it might have played.Trump and his administration have long been open about the deep antipathy they feel for Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish prime minister, whose refusal to allow the US to use its airbases during the Iran war, rejection of the 5% defence spending target and vociferous criticism of Israel’s actions in Gaza have arguably made Spain the administration’s least favourite EU country.The American response seemed to be a triumph for Rabat, whose relationship with the US president traces back to his first term, when Morocco agreed to normalise ties with Israel in exchange for Trump’s recognition of its sovereignty claim over the disputed territory of Western Sahara.Since then, Morocco’s all-powerful monarch had doubled down on outreach efforts, said Fabiani. “The Moroccans have really made extra efforts to cultivate every single major decision-maker within the administration, including the president himself, to make sure that this administration will support, until the end, the Moroccan autonomy plan for Western Sahara.”A hint that the relationship could help Morocco lay claim to more than Western Sahara came in a recent US congressional report that appeared to be sympathetic to Morocco’s refusal to recognise Ceuta as Spanish territory, describing it as “Spanish-administered” rather than a part of Spain, as it has been since 1580.Days after the influx, interest in Ceuta remained heightened among those close to both Trump and the Israeli government, said Haizam Amirah-Fernández, the director of the Madrid-based Centre for Contemporary Arab Studies. “They haven’t stopped talking about Ceuta for several days in a row, which is quite striking.”Red Cross personnel distributing food at Trampolín beach in Ceuta this week. Photograph: REDUAN/EPAWhat had been laid bare was Rabat’s willingness to use “hybrid tactics to achieve political objectives”, said Amirah-Fernández, drawing a parallel with May 2021 when Rabat loosened border controls to allow more than 8,000 people to cross into Ceuta in a show of anger over Madrid’s decision to allow a Western Sahara pro-independence leader to travel to Spain to be treated for Covid-19.This time around, as nearly 10 times more people crossed into Ceuta, it set off a bout of finger-pointing across the EU rather than any kind of concerted effort to push back using the bloc’s status as Morocco’s largest trading partner and largest foreign investor. “The reaction of several governments in the EU was, in the end, what the White House was looking for – the erosion of solidarity between European partners,” said Amirah-Fernández.Senior officials in Morocco have pushed back against accusations it was in any way complicit.King Mohammed VI and Trump in 2018. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty ImagesAt the Rabat-based Moroccan Institute for Policy Analysis, there was little doubt that relations between Morocco and the US were in their “golden era”. Even so, the country’s approach to the Trump administration remained pragmatic, said Said Saddiki, a senior fellow at the institute.“Moroccan policymakers are well aware of President Trump’s transactional style and have sought to preserve Morocco’s strategic autonomy,” Saddiki said in an email
contentParagraphs.zh: 从摩洛哥今年宣布成为第一个加入唐纳德·特朗普和平委员会的非洲国家，到特朗普最近为穆罕默德六世国王执政27周年发来的贺电，华盛顿和拉巴特之间的亲密关系长期以来一直为双方所标榜。最新的例子本周登陆。当西班牙努力应对7万多人突然涌入并迅速返回休达的后果时，摩洛哥国王证实，他以特朗普的名字命名了西撒哈拉争议领土两侧的一条耗资10亿美元的高速公路。随着人们继续质疑到底是什么导致了致命的大规模越境进入北非西班牙狭小领土的问题，不断加深的关系受到新的审视。“我认为有足够的证据来假设或者声称摩洛哥是幕后黑手，”国际危机组织北非项目主任里卡多·法比亚尼 (Riccardo Fabiani) 说。 “但这并没有明确的触发因素，这也是让所有人感到困惑的地方。” 西班牙休达飞地的移民被护送回摩洛哥——视频观察家认为，西班牙最近与拉巴特的主要竞争对手阿尔及利亚的和解可能引发了摩洛哥的局势。但法比亚尼表示，另一种或许更合理的解释指向美国。“这显然不可能证明，”他说。 “但就合理性而言，我不认为不可能想象摩洛哥可能会做一些事情来赢得其盟友的印象，因为摩洛哥和华盛顿的这个特定政府确实有着非常密切、良好的关系。”他说，虽然摩洛哥可能没有“策划”涌入休达的事件，但它与特朗普政府的关系 - 以及摩洛哥国王希望将其对休达的主权置于聚光灯下 - 可能影响了它如何应对快速蔓延的疫情网上有关于西班牙边境开放的传言。周六，一名年轻人在试图进入休达后被西班牙安全部队护送。照片：Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters “摩洛哥安全部队肯定正在监视这些谈话，”法比亚尼说。 “他们看到了这一点，可能进行了一些谈话，他们决定不采取任何行动，看看事态会如何发展。” 随后发生的事情成为全球头条新闻，数以万计的人游泳或涉水跨越欧盟与非洲的两个陆地边界之一。当西班牙忙于应对时，极右翼的声音抓住了这些画面。 在美国，副总统 JD 万斯和国务院将难民涌入归咎于社会党领导的西班牙政府，而特朗普则警告称，当选民主党将使西班牙发生的事情“显得微不足道”。他们中没有人提到摩洛哥或它可能发挥的潜在作用。特朗普和他的政府长期以来一直公开表达他们对西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯的深切反感，桑切斯拒绝允许美国在伊朗战争期间使用其空军基地，拒绝5%的国防开支目标，并大声批评以色列在加沙的行动，可以说使西班牙成为政府最不喜欢的欧盟国家。美国的回应似乎是一次胜利对于拉巴特来说，他与美国总统的关系可以追溯到他的第一个任期，当时摩洛哥同意与以色列实现关系正常化，以换取特朗普承认其对西撒哈拉有争议领土的主权要求。法比亚尼说，从那时起，摩洛哥全能的君主就加倍了外展努力。 “摩洛哥人确实付出了额外的努力来培养政府内部的每一位主要决策者，包括总统本人，以确保本届政府将支持摩洛哥的西撒哈拉自治计划，直到最后。”最近的一份美国国会报告暗示，这种关系可以帮助摩洛哥对西撒哈拉以外的地区提出主权要求，该报告似乎对摩洛哥拒绝承认休达为西班牙领土表示同情，并将其描述为“西班牙管理”，而不是一个西班牙领土。自 1580 年以来，休达一直是西班牙的一部分。马德里当代阿拉伯研究中心主任海扎姆·阿米拉-费尔南德斯表示，在难民涌入几天后，与特朗普和以色列政府关系密切的人对休达的兴趣仍然高涨。 “他们连续几天没有停止谈论休达，这相当引人注目。” 本周，红十字会工作人员在休达的 Trampolín 海滩分发食物。阿米拉-费尔南德斯说，暴露的事实是拉巴特愿意使用“混合策略来实现政治目标”，他将这与 2021 年 5 月的情况进行了比较，当时拉巴特放松了边境管制，允许 8,000 多人进入休达，以表达对马德里决定允许西撒哈拉支持独立领导人前往西班牙接受 Covid-19 治疗的愤怒。越境进入休达的人数增加了近十倍，这引发了整个欧盟的相互指责，而不是任何形式的共同努力来抵制利用欧盟作为摩洛哥最大贸易伙伴和最大外国投资者的地位。阿米拉-费尔南德斯表示：“归根结底，欧盟多个国家政府的反应正是白宫所希望看到的——欧洲伙伴之间的团结受到侵蚀。”摩洛哥高级官员反驳了有关其以任何方式同谋的指控。穆罕默德六世国王和特朗普在 2018 年。照片：卢多维奇·马林/法新社/盖蒂图片社在位于拉巴特的摩洛哥政策分析研究所，毫无疑问，摩洛哥之间的关系正在恶化美国正处于“黄金时代”。即便如此，该国对特朗普政府的态度仍然务实，该研究所高级研究员赛义德·萨迪基表示。“摩洛哥决策者非常了解特朗普总统的交易风格，并寻求维护摩洛哥的战略自主权，”萨迪基在一封电子邮件中表示

articles.title: Government to prioritise job creation in awarding public contracts under new rules
articles.summary: The changes are part of government efforts to tackle the youth unemployment crisis.
articles.titleZh: 根据新规则，政府在授予公共合同时将优先考虑创造就业机会
articles.summaryZh: 这些变化是政府解决青年失业危机努力的一部分。

contentParagraphs.en: Andy Burnham will tell firms bidding for public contracts to prove they are creating jobs rather than meeting green and social targets in a bid to get more people into work.The prime minister will overhaul the £90bn public procurement system so bidders have to show they are supporting young people into work and addressing local skills shortages.It comes as the government seeks to tackle the youth unemployment crisis, with Burnham saying he wants to create "growth in every postcode".But green groups criticised the plans, arguing supporting young people into work should not come at the expense of the environment.Companies bidding for government contracts are judged on a range of measures, including value for money and the extent to which they bring benefits to the local community. Under the changes, the weighting given to the benefits brought by companies will be doubled, from 10% to 20% for contracts worth £5m or more, the Cabinet Office said. Previously, this accounted for how companies created social value through measures such as equality and diversity, net zero and the post-Covid recovery. The new 20% measure will instead be based on job creation. Bidders will be given extra credit for creating local jobs paying above the minimum wage, plugging local skills gaps by offering training and particularly by offering 45-day work experience placements for young people. Office for National Statistics (ONS) figures show more than a million people aged 16 to 24 are currently not in education, employment or training (Neet).Burnham used a similar initiative to oversee a rise in the latter during his time as mayor of Greater Manchester. First Secretary of State Louise Haigh — who is effectively Burnham's deputy prime minister — said the procurement process in its current form was a "tick-box exercise"."Every pound of taxpayer money should be spent in a way that benefits local communities — creating good jobs and giving young people the skills they need for the future," she said.The new model will apply to both British and international firms bidding for public contracts.Haigh said: "These new rules will ensure the £90 billion that is spent each year through government contracts supports British jobs, skills and people in every postcode."Cabinet Office Minister Mark Ferguson said that businesses who secure government contracts "have a responsibility to give back"."Businesses that benefit from the billions of taxpayer pounds spent by government, will have to create more local jobs and opportunities for young people in their area," he said.But Greenpeace UK's head of politics Ami McCarthy said protecting the environment and helping young people into work are "mutually beneficial and one shouldn't come at a cost to the other"."Companies should be held to account with environmental targets to help achieve a better future without leaving young workers behind," she added.
contentParagraphs.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 将告诉竞标公共合同的公司，要证明他们正在创造就业机会，而不是为了让更多人就业而达到绿色和社会目标。首相将彻底改革 900 亿英镑的公共采购体系，因此竞标者必须表明他们正在支持年轻人就业并解决当地技能短缺问题。这是在政府寻求解决青年失业危机之际，伯纳姆表示他希望创造“每个邮政编码的增长”。但绿色组织批评了这些计划，认为支持年轻人就业不应以牺牲环境为代价。竞标政府合同的公司会根据一系列指标进行评判，包括物有所值以及为当地社区带来利益的程度。英国内阁办公室表示，根据这些变化，对于价值 500 万英镑或以上的合同，公司带来的利益的权重将增加一倍，从 10% 增加到 20%。此前，这解释了公司如何通过平等和多样性、净零排放和新冠疫情后复苏等措施创造社会价值。新的 20% 措施将基于创造就业机会。竞标者将因在当地创造高于最低工资的就业机会、通过提供培训、特别是为年轻人提供为期 45 天的工作经验实习来填补当地技能差距而获得额外荣誉。英国国家统计局 (ONS) 的数据显示，目前有超过 100 万 16 至 24 岁的人没有接受教育、就业或培训（尼特族）。伯纳姆在担任大曼彻斯特市长期间，也采取了类似的举措来监督后者的增长。第一国务卿路易丝·黑格（Louise Haigh）——实际上是伯纳姆的副首相——表示，目前形式的采购过程是一个“勾选框练习”。“每一磅纳税人的钱都应该用在有利于当地社区的方式上——创造良好的就业机会，为年轻人提供未来所需的技能，”她说。新模式将适用于竞标公共合同的英国和国际公司。黑格说：“这些新规则将确保每年通过政府合同支出的 900 亿英镑支持英国内阁办公厅部长马克·弗格森表示，获得政府合同的企业“有责任回馈社会”。“从政府花费的数十亿纳税人英镑中受益的企业将必须为所在地区的年轻人创造更多的本地就业机会和机会，”他说。但英国绿色和平组织政治负责人阿米·麦卡锡表示，保护环境和帮助年轻人就业是“互惠互利的，不应以牺牲社会利益为代价”。 “公司应该对环境目标负责，以帮助实现更美好的未来，同时不让年轻工人落后，”她补充道。

articles.title: See the Sun like never before with most detailed images yet
articles.summary: New images and footage of the Sun show "whirlpools" of activity that it has not been possible to see before.
articles.titleZh: 通过迄今为止最详细的图像以前所未有的方式观看太阳
articles.summaryZh: 太阳的新图像和镜头显示了以前不可能看到的活动“漩涡”。

contentParagraphs.en: Figure caption, See through the eyes of the world's most powerful solar telescope as it zooms in on the Sun's surface (NSF/NSO/AURA/MPS)ByVictoria GillScience correspondent Scientists using the world's most powerful solar telescope have captured the surface of our Sun in new, unprecedented detail.Images and footage show "whirlpools" of activity that it has not been possible to see before. It is the Sun's magnetic field being twisted and moved by the motion of hot gas.That constant swirling is a driving force behind bursts of energy from the Sun, creating so-called space weather, that can disrupt Earth's power grids and satellites, and could even injure astronauts. "The Sun is the source of that energy and of all of that space weather," explained Dr David Boboltz from the US National Solar Observatory, external (NSO).Capturing more detailed pictures of our solar system's star will help in responding to that weather, he said. "To figure out and eventually predict space weather, we want to understand the physics of the Sun, all the way down to the smallest scales."Image source, NSF/NSO/AURA/MPSImage caption, These are the highest-resolution images of the Sun's surface, or photosphere, that have ever been capturedThe findings, published in the journal Nature, external, were made possible by the Inouye Solar Telescope - a facility built on a high peak in Hawaii, where clear blue skies are free of dust. Zooming in on the Sun's surface, the team captured a detailed view of swirling vortices. NSO astronomer Dr David Kuridze, told BBC News: "These twisting motions are creating magnetic energy, which can build up to produce those large-scale explosions."Image source, NASA/SDOImage caption, The scientists say they have captured the driving force behind sudden blasts of solar plasma and magnetic fields that the Sun sends into spaceExplosive space weatherThe term for what the scientists have discovered on the Sun is "Kelvin-Helmholtz instability". The phenomenon happens when fluids - in this case hot gases - slide past each other and cause small disturbances to grow into spiralling vortices. In the ocean, it helps explain how ripples become giant, powerful waves.Dr Friedrich Woeger, also from the NSO, explained that finding it on the Sun's surface not only explained the dynamics behind space weather, but even why the surface of the Sun is so hot. It shows how energy is transported upwards. "Once there's enough energy wound up in the higher layers, it can then be released, as a flare or what's known as a coronal mass ejection," he said. Image source, NASAImage caption, An image of the Sun captured by NASA which shows ejectionsBoboltz added that, as well as the practical need to understand and protect ourselves from space weather, the new findings were a reminder that the Sun is a "unique laboratory"."It's our closest star," he said. "And it can help us understand some very basic laws of physics. "The first experimental proof of Einstein's general relativity came from solar eclipse observations."So simply for human knowledge," he added, "we need to have experiments like this".Image source, NSF National Solar ObservatoryImage caption, The NSF Inouye Solar Telescope sits on a high peak, above the clouds
