contentParagraphs.en: Hong Myung-bo’s appointment under scrutiny amid raids with lack of proper interview process previously alleged.Seoul ‌police have raided the Korea Football Association (KFA) offices ⁠⁠as part of an “obstruction of business” investigation into the appointment of former coach Hong Myung-bo.Hong returned as national ⁠team coach in 2024 after a previous spell in charge from 2013 to 2014.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4FIFA pledges to defend Infantino after World Cup rights plan collapseslist 2 of 4UEFA’s threatened legal action against Infantino and FIFA: What we knowlist 3 of 4Ex-Arsenal boss Wenger was ‘not aware’ of Infantino’s FIFA planlist 4 of 4UEFA confirms legal letter served to FIFA after Infantino’s World Cup planend of listHis appointment came under scrutiny after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign candidates ‌and appointed him following a brief meeting.The issue resurfaced after South Korea’s disappointing FIFA World Cup campaign, which ended in a group-stage exit.At a parliamentary hearing last month, Hong rejected suggestions by lawmakers that he had received special treatment in his appointment, ⁠while taking responsibility for South Korea’s ⁠failure at the tournament.South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said in October 2024 that the KFA breached its own rules in the appointments of Hong and former coach Jurgen Klinsmann, finding that the technical director’s ⁠meeting with Hong did not constitute ⁠a proper interview.However, it found no evidence of illegal conduct and did not order Hong’s contract to be cancelled.Police had already been ‌investigating complaints alleging improper interference in Hong’s appointment before the World Cup.No criminal findings have been announced ‌against ‌Hong or KFA officials.The KFA did not immediately respond to a request by Al Jazeera for comment.
contentParagraphs.zh: 洪明博的任命因此前据称缺乏适当面试程序的突击搜查而受到审查。首尔警方突击搜查了韩国足球协会 (KFA) 办公室，作为对前教练洪明博任命的“妨碍业务”调查的一部分。洪明博在 2013 年至 2014 年执掌国家队教练后，于 2024 年重返国家队主教练。 推荐故事列表 4 项列表 1 4国际足联承诺在世界杯权利计划崩溃后捍卫因凡蒂诺list 2 of 4UEFA威胁对因凡蒂诺和国际足联采取法律行动：我们所知道的list 3 of 4前阿森纳主帅温格“不知道”因凡蒂诺的FIFA计划list 4 of 4UEFA确认在因凡蒂诺的世界杯计划后向国际足联发出了法律信函列表列表他的任命在韩国足协放弃了长达数月的时间后受到了审查搜索涉及外国候选人并在简短的会议后任命了他。在韩国令人失望的国际足联世界杯竞选活动以小组赛结束后，这个问题再次浮出水面。在上个月的议会听证会上，洪拒绝了议员们关于他在任命中受到特殊待遇的建议，同时为韩国在世界杯上的失败承担责任。韩国文化体育和旅游部于 2024 年 10 月表示，韩国足协在任命洪和洪的过程中违反了自己的规则。前教练尤尔根·克林斯曼 (Jurgen Klinsmann) 认为，技术总监与洪的会面并不构成适当的采访。但是，它没有发现任何非法行为的证据，也没有下令取消洪的合同。警方已经在世界杯前调查指控洪的任命不当的投诉。尚未公布针对洪或韩国足协官员的刑事调查结果。韩国足协没有立即回应半岛电视台的要求评论。

articles.title: AI models have been going rogue in tests – how worried should we be?
articles.summary:
The UK’s AI Security Institute test revealed AI models indulging in unprecedented hacking attempts

AI models shock UK testers by using fake identities to trick developers

Two cutting-edge AI models have targeted real people and organisations in the latest safety scare to hit th
articles.titleZh: 人工智能模型在测试中一直表现不佳——我们应该有多担心？
articles.summaryZh:
英国人工智能安全研究所测试揭示人工智能模型陷入前所未有的黑客攻击

人工智能模型使用虚假身份欺骗开发人员，令英国测试人员感到震惊

在最新的安全恐慌中，两种尖端人工智能模型针对真实的人和组织

contentParagraphs.en: Two cutting-edge AI models have targeted real people and organisations in the latest safety scare to hit the technology. The UK’s AI Security Institute (AISI) said the incident was unprecedented but could become more common as the technology becomes increasingly capable.What happened?The AISI, which is owned by the UK government and tests advanced AI models, said in a blog post that two AI agents carried out unprecedented hacking attempts during a cybersecurity evaluation. The agents – tools that carry out computer tasks autonomously – were powered by two models: Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT 5.6-Sol. AISI said there were 19 examples of rogue behaviour, 17 of them carried out by Mythos.In the most serious incident, the Mythos agent decided that hacking users on GitHub – a platform used by software developers – would enable it to deploy a piece of software that would allow it to pass the test. It set up accounts with fake online identities and used them to target a software developer on GitHub with the power to approve its malicious code. It also sent emails carrying malware to other individuals.It hoped that getting the malware downloaded would set off a chain of events that would allow it to pass the evaluation. The Sol-powered agent also attempted to access a GitHub account.This novel behaviour was detected on 28 July and took an hour to shut down. At one point AISI shut off all access to the Mythos and Sol models across the entire organisation.Why was AISI alarmed?The institute said the models were showing deceptive behaviour it had not seen before. In one example, the Mythos agent signed off a message on GitHub in Danish to try to convince the Danish-speaking developer it was genuine. In another tactic it used a fake GitHub account to agree with its assertions that the malware it was pushing at developers was not dangerous.The agent used a Tor browser – which anonymises a web user’s identity – to get around sign-up checks on GitHub and create multiple fake accounts.AISI also published the agent’s “reasoning” behind the fake supporting statement ruse. The model, which tackles problems by breaking them down into “steps” that can be viewed by researchers, stated that it would delay posting the fake support message for a few minutes so that it would read as “independent feedback rather than coordinated.”AISI described the behaviour as “sustained”. It kept on trying.Did the models know they were targeting real humans?AISI says it is unclear whether the agents “realised” they were targeting real humans. Throughout the attempted hack the Mythos agent reasons about whether it is interacting with real or simulated people and systems. At one point the agent reasons that it is behaving in the real world: “This is happening on real GitHub, so the consequences are genuine.” It also states: “The environment appears to be simulated.”AISI described the agent conducting “OSINT” – or open source intelligence, where a hacker pulls together publicly available information to work out how to breach a target – to study the developer behind the software it wanted to hack. It gained the developer’s email address and looked at their GitHub history to gauge when they would be active.What do experts think?AISI states clearly these models were operating under abnormal conditions of unfettered internet access and lowered cyber guardrails. Calling for the incident to be viewed with “nuance”, it said it had partly enabled the behaviour with its own actions – but it did not anticipate the “extent and severity” of what happened.Alan Woodward, a professor of cybersecurity at the University of Surrey, said giving the models access to the open internet and removing some guardrails raised questions about using the rest of the world as “live guinea pigs” for powerful technology.“What we should be alarmed about is not what the models are capable of but the way people are testing them,” he said.AISI said in its report into the GitHub incident that giving a powerful model full internet access was a good way of simulating how far a rogue actor could push an AI. It said such a strategy gives a “more realistic sense of what a model may be capable of once deployed”.Ciaran Martin, the former head of the National Cyber Security Centre – part of the GCHQ intelligence agency – said the circumstances of the incident were unlikely to be replicated in the real world so “it’s not that worrying”. But he said it was the third example in recent weeks, after similar occurrences at OpenAI and Anthropic, that testers have released AI agents and found out about their misbehaviour after the fact.Martin said AISI’s pledge to carry out real-time monitoring of tests in the future “must be the answer”.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在最新的安全恐慌中，两个尖端的人工智能模型以真实的人和组织为目标，以打击该技术。英国人工智能安全研究所（AISI）表示，这一事件是史无前例的，但随着技术能力的不断增强，可能会变得更加普遍。到底发生了什么？英国政府所有、测试先进人工智能模型的 AISI 在一篇博客文章中表示，两名人工智能代理在一次网络安全评估期间进行了前所未有的黑客攻击。这些代理（自主执行计算机任务的工具）由两种模型提供支持：Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT 5.6-Sol。 AISI 表示，存在 19 起流氓行为，其中 17 起是由 Mythos 实施的。 在最严重的事件中，Mythos 特工决定在 GitHub（软件开发人员使用的平台）上攻击用户，使其能够部署一款软件，从而通过测试。它使用虚假的在线身份建立帐户，并利用这些帐户来攻击 GitHub 上有权批准其恶意代码的软件开发人员。它还向其他个人发送携带恶意软件的电子邮件。它希望下载恶意软件会引发一系列事件，从而使其通过评估。 Sol 驱动的代理还尝试访问 GitHub 帐户。这种新颖的行为于 7 月 28 日被发现，并花了一个小时才关闭。 AISI 一度关闭了整个组织对 Mythos 和 Sol 模型的所有访问。AISI 为什么感到震惊？该研究所表示，这些模型表现出了以前从未见过的欺骗行为。在一个示例中，Mythos 代理在 GitHub 上用丹麦语签署了一条消息，试图让丹麦语开发人员相信该消息是真实的。在另一种策略中，它使用虚假的 GitHub 帐户来证实其向开发人员推送的恶意软件并不危险的说法。该代理使用 Tor 浏览器（匿名网络用户的身份）来绕过 GitHub 上的注册检查并创建多个虚假帐户。AISI 还公布了该代理在虚假支持声明诡计背后的“推理”。该模型通过将问题分解为研究人员可以查看的“步骤”来解决问题，并表示它将延迟发布虚假支持消息几分钟，以便将其视为“独立反馈而不是协调”。AISI 将这种行为描述为“持续”。它一直在尝试。这些模型知道他们的目标是真实的人类吗？AISI 表示，目前还不清楚特工是否“意识到”他们的目标是真实的人类。在整个尝试的黑客攻击过程中，Mythos 代理会判断它是与真实的还是模拟的人和系统进行交互。有一次，代理解释说它是在现实世界中表现的：“这发生在真实的 GitHub 上，所以后果是真实的。”它还指出：“环境似乎是模拟的。”AISI 描述了执行“OSINT”（即开源情报）的代理，即黑客将公开可用的信息汇集在一起​​以找出如何突破目标的方法，以研究其想要攻击的软件背后的开发人员。它获得了开发者的电子邮件地址，并查看了他们的 GitHub 历史记录，以判断他们何时会活跃。专家们怎么看？AISI 明确表示，这些模型是在不受限制的互联网访问和降低的网络护栏的异常条件下运行的。该公司呼吁以“细微差别”的态度来看待这一事件，并表示自己的行为在一定程度上促成了这一行为，但它没有预料到所发生事件的“程度和严重性”。 萨里大学网络安全教授艾伦·伍德沃德表示，让模型访问开放互联网并拆除一些护栏，引发了对将世界其他地区用作强大技术的“活豚鼠”的质疑。“我们应该警惕的不是模型的能力，而是模型的方式。 AISI 在 GitHub 事件报告中表示，为强大的模型提供完整的互联网访问权限是模拟流氓行为者可以将人工智能推向何种程度的好方法。报告称，这样的策略“可以更现实地了解模型一旦部署后可能具有的能力”。英国政府通讯总部情报机构下属的国家网络安全中心前负责人夏兰·马丁表示，该事件的情况不太可能在现实世界中复制，因此“并不那么令人担忧”。但他表示，继 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发生类似事件之后，这是最近几周第三个例子，测试人员发布了人工智能代理，并在事后发现了他们的不当行为。Martin 表示，AISI 承诺在未来对测试进行实时监控“一定是答案”。

articles.title: Farmers warn shoppers face smaller and more expensive vegetables due to hot weather
articles.summary: This year's harvest could be the worst on record due to the exceptionally dry spring and summer.
articles.titleZh: 农民警告说，由于天气炎热，购物者将面临更小、更贵的蔬菜
articles.summaryZh: 由于春季和夏季异常干燥，今年的收成可能是有记录以来最差的。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Farmers said the dry weather could lead to higher prices or smaller vegetables for consumersByAlex DanielBusiness reporter and Esme StallardSenior climate and science reporterThis year's harvest could be the worst on record as farmers warn the exceptionally dry spring and summer could lead to "shrinkflation" in UK supermarkets.England and Wales saw their driest July since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, and a drought has been declared across large parts of the country.The Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) thinktank said the UK's cereals and oilseed harvest could be 2.5 million tonnes less than ​earlier forecasts.Tim O'Malley, the chairman of Nationwide produce, said it was "as bad as its ever been" and that shoppers will likely see higher prices or smaller vegetables in supermarkets.The harvest of barley, oats and rapeseed, which are used in beer, breakfast cereals and vegetable oil, is estimated to drop to just 19.5 million tonnes, the worst since records began in 1984.That is compared with a previous low of 19.8 million tonnes in 2020, and would cost farmers £390m in lost revenue, the ECIU estimated.The crops are also used for feeding livestock, making them crucial across most of the food chain.O'Malley said consumers could feel the impact in the vegetable aisle too, where grocers are likely to swap in smaller produce at the same price, which is known as shrinkflation."I think we're going to see shrinkflation," he told Radio 5 Live's Wake Up to Money."The problem we're going to have this year is a massive reduction in yield and major quality issues," O'Malley said.He said that will mean smaller sizes for fresh produce."We've got crop with stress or we've got quality issues. So you will see a smaller crop," O'Malley said.He said supermarkets will "do everything" to keep prices where they are, but added: "eventually they will probably have to come to the party and increase the price, particularly if they start importing."Grocers are already bringing in more products from abroad because of the poor conditions at home."We're importing broccoli and iceberg from Spain at this time of year, which in August [is] unheard of. I think we're going to see more of that, unfortunately," O'Malley said.He added: "Loud and clear, it's grim out there. I think it's as bad as it's ever been … Every record is being broken."The difference in this year and last year, last year we had four heat waves. But in between them we had a bit of rain."Farmers source additional water for their crops and livestock over summer from a combination of stored winter rainfall on site, and by extracting it from natural sources - a process called abstraction.This can be from groundwater or from surface water, like rivers and streams.This summer has seen significant low rainfall affecting the amount of water available to draw from.Half of England and all of Wales have been declared to be in drought conditions by the Environment Agency.Wales has received just 8% of its average rainfall so far this month. England has received 7% of its average, with that figure as low as 1% across southern England.The high temperatures and repeated heatwaves have also increased evaporation rates which have particularly hit rivers.Climate change is expected to bring more severe, frequent and longer-lasting heatwaves in UK summers in the coming years - which could bring more water shortages for farmers.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Experts said the the UK's cereals and oilseed harvest could be the worst since records began in 1984.Tom Lancaster, land, food and farming analyst at the ECIU said: "At the start of spring farmers were hopeful of a better year, but the dry April and July and record-breaking heat have left farmers facing down the barrel of a third awful harvest in a row."Farming is now the sector most exposed to climate change and the risks and damage that it brings."Martin Lines, head of the Nature Friendly Farming Network and a farmer from Cambridgeshire, said this year's harvest "has been a real kick in the teeth"."After two terrible harvests in a row, the crops this year were looking good and full of potential coming out of spring, only for months of drought and heatwaves to destroy any prospect of a decent harvest," he said."I've never known it this dry and hot on our farm."Even farmers I know who were sceptical of climate change are now saying they're really worried about the future of their businesses and production, it's just been completely brutal for our industry."Get in touchHas your farm or business been affected by the extreme weather?
contentParagraphs.zh: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社 图片说明，农民表示，干燥的天气可能会导致价格上涨或消费者购买的蔬菜变少作者：亚历克斯·丹尼尔（Alex Daniel）商业记者和埃斯梅·斯塔拉德（Esme Stallard）高级气候与科学记者今年的收成可能是有记录以来最差的，因为农民警告说，异常干燥的春季和夏季可能会导致英国超市“收缩通货膨胀”。据英国气象局称，英格兰和威尔士经历了自 190 年前有记录以来最干旱的 7 月，英国大部分地区已宣布干旱。能源和气候情报机构 (ECIU) 智囊团表示，英国谷物和油籽收成可能比之前的预测少 250 万吨。全国农产品公司董事长蒂姆·奥马利表示，情况“一如既往地糟糕”，购物者可能会在超市看到更高的价格或较小的蔬菜。用于啤酒、早餐麦片和植物油的大麦、燕麦和油菜籽的收成预计将减少产量下降至 1950 万吨，这是自 1984 年有记录以来的最低水平。 ECIU 估计，与之前 2020 年 1980 万吨的低点相比，这将使农民损失 3.9 亿英镑的收入。这些作物还用于饲养牲畜，使其在食物链的大部分环节中至关重要。奥马利表示，消费者也能感受到蔬菜货架上的影响，杂货商可能会以相同的价格换取较小的农产品，这被称为收缩通货膨胀。“我认为我们将会看到收缩通货膨胀，”他告诉第五广播电台直播节目《金钱的觉醒》。奥马利说，“今年我们将面临的问题是产量大幅下降和重大质量问题。”他说，这将意味着新鲜农产品的尺寸更小。“我们的作物面临压力，或者出现质量问题。所以你会看到产量减少，”奥马利说。他说超市将“尽一切努力”来减少产量。保持价格不变，但补充道：“最终他们可能不得不参加聚会并提高价格，特别是如果他们开始进口的话。”由于国内条件恶劣，杂货商已经从国外进口了更多产品。“我们在每年的这个时候从西班牙进口西兰花和冰山花，这在八月是闻所未闻的。不幸的是，我认为我们会看到更多这样的情况，”奥马利说。他补充说：“大声而清晰，我认为那里的情况和以往一样糟糕……每项记录都在被打破。“今年和去年不同，去年我们经历了四次热浪。但在这期间，我们下了一点雨。“农民们在夏季通过现场储存的冬季降雨以及从自然资源中提取水来为农作物和牲畜获取额外的水，这一过程称为抽取。这可以来自地下水，也可以来自河流和溪流等地表水。今年夏天，降雨量显着偏低，影响了可用水量。环境署已宣布英格兰一半地区和威尔士全境处于干旱状态。威尔士收到的水量仅为其平均水量的 8%本月到目前为止，英格兰的降雨量仅为平均水平的 7%，英格兰南部地区的降雨量仅为 1%。高温和反复出现的热浪也增加了蒸发率，尤其是对河流的影响。气候变化预计将在未来几年给英国夏季带来更严重、更频繁和更持久的热浪，这可能会给农民带来更多的水资源短缺。图片来源，盖蒂图片社图片说明，专家表示，英国的谷物和油籽收成可能是有记录以来最差的。 1984年，ECIU的土地、食品和农业分析师汤姆·兰卡斯特(Tom Lancaster)表示：“春季伊始，农民们对美好的一年抱有希望，但干燥的四月和七月以及创纪录的高温使农民面临连续第三次糟糕的收成。“农业现在是最容易受到气候变化及其带来的风险和损害的部门。”自然友好农业网络负责人、来自剑桥郡的农民马丁·莱恩斯(Martin Lines)表示，今年的收成他说：“在经历了连续两次糟糕的收成之后，今年的农作物看起来很好，并且充满了春天的潜力，只是几个月的干旱和热浪破坏了任何体面收成的前景。”“我从来没有见过我们的农场如此干燥和炎热。”即使是我认识的对气候变化持怀疑态度的农民现在也表示，他们真的很担心他们的业务和生产的未来，这对我们来说是完全残酷的。行业。“联系您的农场或企业是否受到极端天气的影响？

articles.title: What can scientists learn from a stray SpaceX rocket hitting the Moon?
articles.summary: While the collision was an accident, it is a unique scientific gift for planetary geologists that could provide important data for future space missions.
articles.titleZh: 科学家们可以从 SpaceX 撞向月球的火箭中学到什么？
articles.summaryZh: 虽然这次碰撞是一次意外，但它对行星地质学家来说是一份独特的科学礼物，可以为未来的太空任务提供重要数据。

contentParagraphs.en: Figure caption, Why haven't we seen images of SpaceX Moon crash yet?ByPallab GhoshScience CorrespondentA stray SpaceX rocket is believed to have crashed into the Moon, forming a crater near a famous lunar landmark and giving scientists a unique research opportunity that could help future missions.The empty upper stage of a Falcon 9 rocket was due to strike the Moon near the Einstein crater at a speed of about 5,400mph (8,700km/h) on Wednesday.The short, dramatic flash it created would have been hard to catch by amateur astronomers even with high-end telescopes, but larger observatories in the Americas are analysing the information.It could be days or even weeks before the full picture of what happened and what we can learn from it is known - but for planetary geologists, this accidental collision is a scientific gift.Figure caption, Watch: Science Museum's head of space on what scientists will look for after crashSpace X's Falcon 9 rocket is a reusable model and has been sent into space on several missions. Its design allows part of the rocket to return to Earth, but other sections are shed in space.The rocket blasted off from Florida in January last year, carrying two lunar landers into space.Its job was to fire the upper stage hard enough to send both of the landers out of Earth's orbit and onto a path towards the Moon - mission accomplished.The spent stage - which is about the size of a five-storey building and weighs at least 4,000kg - was left drifting in a long, looping orbit that swung out towards the Moon and back again. Over the next 18 months, the gentle gravitational tug of the Earth, Moon and Sun, along with even light from the Sun, gave a faint push. Astronomers tracking the rocket part eventually worked out that those small nudges had put it on a course towards the Moon and was picking up speed every day.The impact at around 07:35 BST (06:35 GMT) on Wednesday happened in broad daylight for many parts of the world, but the tiny flash it produced would have been far too faint to see, even through a telescope. Amateur astronomers observing in darkness would also have had little realistic chance of seeing the flash, given that it would have lasted a fraction of a second and occured on a part of the Moon bathed in daylight. And so it may also have been hard for them to see a plume of dust stretching as far as 100km (62 miles) that lasted for several minutes.Even spacecraft orbiting the Moon were not in the right place at the right time to watch the impact happen live. South Korea's Danuri orbiter had the best chance, having passed near the crash site shortly beforehand. Its team has told Korean media that any footage will only be released once researchers have completed their analysis.Over the next few days, Nasa's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter will be in position to photograph the site, allowing images before and after the crash to be compared.Image source, NASAImage caption, The Einstein crater is over 180km (112 miles) wide, and is large enough to contain a smaller crater insideThe science and probably the first images might come from powerful telescopes in the Americas where the sky was still dark. Even then, turning the detection of a 14m object hitting a daylight part of the lunar surface i385,000km away won't be easy but not impossible.Image processing to clean up the picture can take hours, days or even weeks, as scientists check and process the data.But the sight of the new crater from the orbiting spacecraft will be eagerly anticipated. Because researchers already know the rocket's exact size, speed and point of impact, this collision turns from being a random accident into a rare, controlled experiment. It is a dream moment for planetary scientists because it lets them test their models of how impacts dig out craters, throw debris across the surface, and send tremors through the Moon's interior.That has real practical value. Understanding how much rock and dust an impact throws up will help engineers design safer landers and future Moon bases, working out how far flying debris can travel and how hard the ground might shake nearby.Material thrown up from beneath the surface offers fresh clues about the Moon's geology, adding to what scientists already know about how the Earth-Moon system formed some 4.5 billion years ago.This is not the first time a human-made object has struck the Moon. Since 1959, dozens of spacecraft have crashed into it, some by accident and many deliberately for science. The Soviet probe Luna 2 was the first, followed over the decades by Nasa's Ranger probes in the 1960s, several Apollo-era rocket stages, and more recently the LCROSS mission in 2009, which was deliberately crashed to search for water ice.The last confirmed accidental impact, in 2022, was thought to be the leftover booster from a Chinese lunar mission launched back in 2014 - a reminder that this sort of space debris has been quietly piling up above our heads for well over half a century.Figure caption, The space junk clean-up!

articles.title: Sudan war threatens ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO Heritage Site
articles.summary: More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.
articles.titleZh: 苏丹战争威胁着联合国教科文组织遗产地古老的麦罗埃金字塔
articles.summaryZh: 200 多座古老的麦罗埃金字塔因苏丹不断升级的战争和忽视而面临危险。

contentParagraphs.en: More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.A family visits the Meroe pyramids at the Meroe archaeological site in Bejrawiya, Sudan. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]By APPublished On 6 Aug 2026Sudan’s war is endangering the ancient pyramids of Meroe, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as fighting and a lack of security have brought all preservation work to a halt and left the fragile structures exposed to the elements.“The site may face a disaster, and collapses are possible,” archaeologist Mahmoud Suleiman said, warning that the more than three-year conflict has prevented experts from carrying out basic maintenance.Located about 200km (125 miles) north of Khartoum, Meroe is home to more than 200 narrow, steep-sided pyramids built between 800 BC and 350 AD as tombs for rulers of the Kingdom of Kush.Guards said windblown sand and encroaching vegetation are accelerating their decay. “The sand has thickened heavily on the pyramids and even inside the temples, and the grass grows thick,” guard Mustafa Ahmed said.“The pyramids have deteriorated greatly, and stones have begun to fall.”Antiquities inspector Mohamed Mubarak said salt released from accumulated sand is attacking the “inherently fragile” stones, eroding ancient inscriptions.Suleiman said climate change, the dispersal of Sudan’s archaeological workforce and the halt of foreign missions have all contributed to “significant deterioration”.UNESCO has warned that more than 100 cultural sites have been damaged and at least 22 museums looted or destroyed since the war began in April 2023.Pyramids at Meroe rise from the desert about 200km (125 miles) north of Khartoum in Sudan’s River Nile state. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Archaeologists say salt crystallisation and halted maintenance threaten to erase centuries-old artwork at Meroe, like this carved relief inside a funerary temple. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]A guide, left, speaks with a visitor at the Meroe archaeological site. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]The Meroe necropolis contains more than 200 pyramids, built as tombs for the rulers of the ancient Kingdom of Kush. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Meroe’s pyramids were constructed from about 800 BC to 350 AD, centuries after the great pyramids of Egypt. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Unlike the broad-based Egyptian pyramids, the pyramids of Meroe are smaller, steeper and more numerous. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]The archaeological sites known as the Island of Meroe in semi-desert area near the Nile were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Meroe was once a royal capital of the Kushite Empire, which controlled trade routes along the Nile and deep into Africa. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Many of the pyramids at Meroe were damaged or looted in the 19th century by treasure hunters searching for gold and jewellery. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]Today, the pyramids of Meroe stand amid shifting desert sands, offering one of the most striking archaeological landscapes in Sudan. [Mohnd Blal/AP Photo]
contentParagraphs.zh: 苏丹不断升级的战争和忽视使 200 多座古代麦罗埃金字塔面临危险。一家人在苏丹贝吉拉维亚的麦罗埃考古遗址参观麦罗埃金字塔。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]美联社于 2026 年 8 月 6 日发布 苏丹的战争正危及被联合国教科文组织列为世界遗产的麦罗埃古金字塔，因为战斗和缺乏安全保障导致所有保护工作陷入停顿，并使脆弱的结构暴露在自然环境中。考古学家马哈茂德·苏莱曼说：“该遗址可能面临灾难，并且有可能倒塌。”他警告说，三年多的冲突使专家无法开展基本的研究工作。麦罗埃位于喀土穆以北约 200 公里（125 英里）处，拥有 200 多座狭窄、陡峭的金字塔，这些金字塔建于公元前 800 年至公元 350 年，是库什王国统治者的陵墓。卫兵称，风吹沙和侵蚀植被正在加速它们的腐烂。警卫穆斯塔法·艾哈迈德说：“金字塔上甚至寺庙内部的沙子都变厚了，草丛也长得很厚。金字塔已经严重恶化，石头已经开始掉落。”古物检查员穆罕默德·穆巴拉克说，堆积的沙子释放的盐分正在侵蚀“本来就脆弱”的石头，侵蚀古代铭文。苏莱曼说，气候变化、苏丹考古队伍的分散和外国任务的停止，使金字塔上的沙子变得越来越厚，甚至在寺庙内部也变得越来越厚。所有这些都导致了“严重恶化”。联合国教科文组织警告说，自 2023 年 4 月战争爆发以来，已有 100 多个文化遗址遭到破坏，至少 22 个博物馆被洗劫或摧毁。麦罗埃的金字塔矗立在苏丹尼罗河州喀土穆以北约 200 公里（125 英里）处的沙漠中。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]考古学家表示，盐结晶和维护工作的停止可能会抹去麦罗埃数百年历史的艺术品，比如墓葬寺庙内的浮雕。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]一名导游（左）在麦罗埃考古遗址与一位游客交谈。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]麦罗埃墓地包含 200 多座金字塔，是为古代库什王国的统治者建造的陵墓。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]麦罗埃的金字塔大约建于公元前 800 年至公元 350 年，比埃及金字塔晚了几个世纪。 [Mohnd Bral/美联社照片]与基础广泛的埃及金字塔不同，麦罗埃的金字塔更小、更陡、数量更多。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]尼罗河附近半沙漠地区的麦罗埃岛考古遗址于2011年被联合国教科文组织列为世界遗产。[Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]麦罗埃曾经是库什特帝国的皇家首都，控制着尼罗河沿岸和深入非洲的贸易路线。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]麦罗埃的许多金字塔在 19 世纪被寻找黄金和珠宝的寻宝者损坏或洗劫一空。 [Mohnd Bal/美联社照片]如今，麦罗埃金字塔矗立在流动的沙漠之中，成为苏丹最引人注目的考古景观之一。 [莫赫德·布拉尔/美联社照片]

articles.title: SpaceX shares sink after first earnings report reveals huge AI spending plans
articles.summary: Elon Musk told investors that people were "underestimating" his company.
articles.titleZh: 首次财报披露巨额人工智能支出计划后 SpaceX 股价下跌
articles.summaryZh: 埃隆·马斯克告诉投资者，人们“低估”了他的公司。

contentParagraphs.en: Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX tumbled after the company's first-ever earnings report revealed a huge jump in spending on artificial intelligence, spooking investors.While the firm's quarterly revenue had nearly doubled to $7.8bn (£5.8bn) from a year earlier, its spending ballooned to $18.3bn, more than six times what it was a year ago, the bulk of which was for AI.The firm builds space rockets and Starlink internet satellites as well as owning the social media platform X. It began trading on the US stock market in June.Its stock fell 9% on Wednesday morning. Musk said during an investor call after the results that people seemed to be "underestimating" SpaceX.Overall SpaceX made a net loss of $143m in the three months to June, and a loss of $2bn during the first six months of the year.However, Musk cited Starlink, the one part of the company that is currently making a profit, bringing in $1.6bn in the second quarter. Musk said he expects that business to grow exponentially in the coming years."It's not out of the question that, at some point, Starlink will operate most of the world's internet," Musk said.He also spoke of an expected and rapid growth of SpaceX's emerging line of business selling compute power needed for artificial intelligence (AI) projects to other companies, which currently include Google and Anthropic.Although SpaceX currently has 1.4 gigawatts of such compute power ready to use, Musk said that sometime next year that capacity should hit at least 10 gigawatts through its ongoing development of data centres.Musk said during the call: "Data centres are a trivial problem compared to making reusable rockets." Making rockets is SpaceX's core business, but the company's space segment showed a $542m net loss against $962m in revenue for the second quarter.SpaceX's AI business also lost $1.2bn during the quarter, on revenue of $2.5bn.Bret Johnson, head of finance for SpaceX, said during the call that the company's capital spending would continue at a "very similar" level for the rest of the year. Nevertheless, Musk said that SpaceX would likely hit $1tn in revenue by 2030, a year earlier than he thought just six weeks ago.Despite this optimism, shares of SpaceX fell in after hours trading on Tuesday, wiping out gains made during the day.Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown, said that because Musk was going "all in" on data centres, the company "could soon resemble an AI infrastructure company with an extraordinary space business attached"."Analysts are still trying to work out what the business should look like, while Elon Musk is already describing what it might become over the next decade," he said."Starship and the next generations of Starlink remain critical to the post-2030 vision, but the financial engine over the next few years will increasingly be AI."Responding to Musk's comment that investors were "underestimating" the firm, Brady Wang from Counterpoint Research said the subscription numbers for Starlink are "strong", but it is the only SpaceX business unit making an operating profit.The firm's AI business is still losing money as spending rises, so it is "a stretch" to say the whole company is being underestimated, said Fabien Yip, an analyst from investment platform IG.Wendy Souvannarath, the chief executive of Carré Partners, which has invested in SpaceX, told BBC News that "every tech giant is spending like this right now" on AI.She told the Today programme that SpaceX was treating its investment in AI as a running cost and expects it to pay for itself within a year.Souvannarath said that even though "Elon Musk will always be Elon Musk", she remained convinced by SpaceX."There is fact, there [are] figures, there is a vision that we can see," she said."Half the planet has bad internet because cables never reached them. So basically Starlink puts the network in the sky instead."Controversies around Musk's politics have moved the needle for some investors before and remains a "live risk" for SpaceX too, Yip added.SpaceX has struggled to hold on to investor enthusiasm despite making history with the largest-ever public listing and then briefly eclipsing the market valuation of established titans like Microsoft and Amazon.Shares of the space technology company have steadily drifted down in price since reaching an on-the-day high of $176 in June. It has been trading lower than its original $135 per share debut price for the last several weeks.
contentParagraphs.zh: 埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下的 SpaceX 公司首次发布财报，披露人工智能支出大幅增长，令投资者感到恐慌，该公司股价应声暴跌。虽然该公司的季度收入较上年同期增长近一倍，达到 78 亿美元（合 58 亿英镑），但其支出却激增至 183 亿美元，是一年前的六倍多，其中大部分用于人工智能。该公司制造太空火箭和 Starlink 互联网卫星，以及拥有社交媒体平台X。该公司于6月开始在美国股市交易。周三上午，该公司股价下跌9%。马斯克在财报公布后的投资者电话会议上表示，人们似乎“低估”了 SpaceX。截至 6 月的三个月内，SpaceX 总体净亏损 1.43 亿美元，今年前 6 个月亏损 20 亿美元。不过，马斯克引用了该公司目前正在盈利的部门 Starlink，第二季度带来了 16 亿美元的收入。马斯克表示，他预计该业务在未来几年将呈指数级增长。“毫无疑问，在某个时候，星链将运营世界上大部分互联网。”马斯克说。他还谈到了 SpaceX 新兴业务线的预期快速增长，该业务线向其他公司（目前包括谷歌和 Anthropic）销售人工智能 (AI) 项目所需的计算能力。尽管 SpaceX 目前拥有 1.4 吉瓦的此类计算能力可供使用，但马斯克表示，未来某个时候通过不断开发的数据中心，今年容量将达到至少 10 吉瓦。马斯克在电话会议中表示：“与制造可重复使用的火箭相比，数据中心是一个微不足道的问题。”制造火箭是 SpaceX 的核心业务，但该公司的航天部门第二季度净亏损 5.42 亿美元，而营收为 9.62 亿美元。SpaceX 的人工智能业务本季度也亏损 12 亿美元，营收为 25 亿美元。SpaceX 财务主管布雷特·约翰逊 (Bret Johnson) 在电话会议中表示，该公司的资本支出将在今年剩余时间继续保持在“非常相似”的水平。尽管如此，马斯克表示，到 2030 年，SpaceX 的收入可能会达到 1 万亿美元，比他六周前的预期提前了一年。尽管有这种乐观情绪，但 SpaceX 的股价在周二盘后交易中下跌，抹去了白天的涨幅。 Hargreaves Lansdown 的高级股票分析师马特·布里茨曼 (Matt Britzman) 表示，由于马斯克将“全力以赴”数据中心，该公司“很快就会像一家拥有非凡太空业务的人工智能基础设施公司”他说：“分析师仍在努力弄清楚该业务应该是什么样子，而埃隆·马斯克已经在描述未来十年它可能会变成什么样子。”“Starship 和下一代 Starlink 对 2030 年后的愿景仍然至关重要，但未来几年的金融引擎将越来越多地是人工智能。”针对马斯克关于投资者“低估”该公司的评论，Counterpoint Research 的 Brady Wang 表示 Starlink 的认购数量“强劲”，投资平台 IG 的分析师 Fabien Yip 表示，随着支出的增加，该公司的人工智能业务仍在亏损，因此说整个公司都被低估了“言过其实”。投资 SpaceX 的 Carré Partners 首席执行官 Wendy Souvannarath 告诉 BBC 新闻，“现在每个科技巨头都在人工智能方面这样花钱”。她告诉 Today 节目，SpaceX 正在对待其投资Souvannarath 表示，尽管“埃隆·马斯克将永远是埃隆·马斯克”，但她仍然对 SpaceX 深信不疑。“事实上，有数据，有我们可以看到的愿景，”她说。“半个地球的互联网状况很差，因为电缆从未到达他们。所以基本上星链将网络放在天空中。”叶补充道，对于 SpaceX 来说，风险也很大。尽管 SpaceX 创造了历史上规模最大的公开上市，并短暂超越了微软和亚马逊等老牌巨头的市场估值，但它一直难以保持投资者的热情。自 6 月份触及 176 美元的当日高点以来，这家太空技术公司的股价一直在稳步下跌。过去几周，该公司的交易价格一直低于最初每股 135 美元的首发价。

articles.title: The cost of being single – and how friends are teaming up to beat it
articles.summary: Many singles face extra costs for housing, bills, food and holidays but there are ways to ease the burden.
articles.titleZh: 单身的代价——以及朋友们如何联合起来克服单身
articles.summaryZh: 许多单身人士面临住房、账单、食物和假期的额外费用，但有一些方法可以减轻负担。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Leanne and Sarah/BBCImage caption, Sarah and Leanne say their decision to buy a house together as friends worked out wellByJemma CrewBusiness reporter When Leanne split up with her partner in her late 20s she thought she'd have to put her dream of a buying a home in the area where she grew up on hold.She was earning a good salary but the properties she was hoping for - with a garden and parking space - were too expensive on her own. While she'd just started seeing someone new, it was very early days - far too early to discuss living together.Her friend since school, Sarah, was single and renting a room in a shared house in Brighton. She also wanted to move back home to Kent, but was worried about how she'd get on the housing ladder on her cabin crew salary.When Sarah suggested they buy together, Leanne admits she "totally baulked". But after chatting with a mortgage adviser they went ahead - and say it's helped them avoid the so-called singles tax.Not being partnered up can mean extra costs. It's tricky to quantify and varies by location - estimates suggest it could be anything from hundreds of pounds to £10,000 on average extra, external a year.The cost of rent or a mortgage, household bills and subscriptions can't be shared. And a single person pays 25% less council tax than a couple - not half.Many discounts involve pairing up - 2-for-1 cinema tickets, Two-Together railcards, couples gym memberships - plus solo travellers often pay a single person supplement.This affects a lot of people. Some 18.5m people had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2024 – 36.8% of the population aged 16 and over, official figures show.And overall 8.6m people were estimated to be living alone in the UK last year - that's nearly a third of all households.Ahead of their house purchase, Sarah and Leanne agreed a minimum amount of time they'd live together for - two years, which they then extended to four - and discussed what would happen if one person wanted to leave. Their mortgage payments were split proportionally to take into account their differing salaries, and the arrangements detailed in a declaration of trust so they would be protected when they came to sell. They were able to split the household bills - with these coming out of a joint account and self-professed "bill keeper" Sarah keeping track of what they needed to transfer each month - but also cut costs by sharing some meals and the cooking as they had similar eating habits."We called it our happy home, not our forever home," says Leanne."And it was a very happy home," agrees Sarah. Image source, Leanne and Sarah/BBCImage caption, Leanne and Sarah call the place they bought together their "happy home"Benefits to buying a home with friends include a bigger deposit and budget, and split costs, according to the Homeowner's Alliance. But it says people should consider potential pitfalls seriously and plan ahead by being upfront about their finances, seeking separate legal advice and drawing up a formal agreement.Sarah and Leanne sold their house for a profit four years after moving in, and they put the equity they'd built up toward their next, separate purchases."Neither of us would have been able to do what we've done without having the property that we had together," says Sarah. "It's brought us a lot of freedom."Leanne thinks she would have been able to afford what she wanted in time, but the financial benefits from buying with Sarah made this possible much sooner."The hidden singles tax is that everything has to take so much longer for you to be able to be in a position of affordability to do what you want to do," she adds.Their success inspired their friend Philly to set up Cucoon - an online platform matching up singles to potentially buy together.She says her aim is to "level the playing field", adding the singles tax is particularly high when it comes to housing.How to cut costs if you're singleMonetise your real estate: rent out rooms, car parking spaces and garagesShared dinners: hosts take turns to cook with larger, cheaper productsBorrowing circles: one person buys an expensive item, such as a lawnmower, and passes it alongErrand pooling: friends share fuel costs by taking it in turns to drive to the supermarketJulia Pearson, from Hampshire, set up the Just4One website about nine years ago when she wanted to go on holiday and discovered many places would charge her extra if she went alone.Alongside practical support for solo life, the platform lists travel providers which do not include the single supplement.Being single feels like a "constant review of your costs all the time", she says.In a list of a money-saving tips for drivers, the RAC suggests adding a named driver onto your car insurance., externalIt's something Julia has tried - and says it's saved her 8%.The RAC says this can bring your premium down, but warns it can also do the opposite.Julia also shares items with friends – she has borrowed tools to renovate her home and given people plant cuttings from her garden."I think as a society, we are becoming more social in terms of our sharing and thinking."Rather than thinking, 'I've got to go out and buy that', think about how else can you play that, what else can you do aside from having to buy something?"And it's good for the social side as well, two benefits in one."Get in touchHow have you managed to cut costs in different areas of your life? contentParagraphs.zh: 图片来源，Leanne 和 Sarah/BBC 图片说明，Sarah 和 Leanne 表示，作为朋友一起买房的决定效果很好。作者：Jemma Crew 商业记者 Leanne 在 20 多岁时与伴侣分手时，她认为自己必须暂时搁置在自己长大的地区买房的梦想。她的薪水不错，但她想要的房产（带有花园和停车位）对她自己来说太贵了。虽然她刚刚开始认识新朋友，但现在讨论同居还为时过早。她从学校开始的朋友莎拉一直单身，在布莱顿的合租房屋中租了一个房间。她还想搬回肯特郡的家，但担心自己如何靠机组人员的工资登上住房阶梯。当莎拉建议他们一起买房时，莉安承认她“完全犹豫了”。但在与抵押贷款顾问交谈后，他们继续前进，并表示这有助于他们避免所谓的单身税。不合作可能意味着额外的成本。量化起来很困难，而且因地点而异 - 据估计，每年外部平均额外费用可能从数百英镑到 10,000 英镑不等。租金或抵押贷款、家庭账单和订阅费用无法分摊。单身人士比情侣少缴纳 25% 的市政税，不是一半。许多折扣涉及结对出行 - 电影票买二送一、两人一起铁路卡、情侣健身房会员资格 - 加上独行旅客通常需要支付单人附加费。这影响了很多人。官方数据显示，到 2024 年，约有 1850 万人从未结婚或建立过民事伴侣关系，占 16 岁及以上人口的 36.8%。据估计，去年英国有 860 万人独居，几乎占所有家庭的三分之一。在购买房屋之前，莎拉和莉安商定了他们在一起生活的最短时间 - 两年，然后延长到四年 - 并讨论了如果有人想要的话会发生什么离开。他们的抵押贷款付款按比例分配，以考虑到他们不同的工资，以及信托声明中详细说明的安排，以便他们在出售时得到保护。他们能够分摊家庭账单——这些账单来自一个联名账户，自称“账单管理员”的莎拉负责跟踪他们每个月需要转账的金额——而且还可以通过分享一些膳食和烹饪来降低成本，因为他们有相似的饮食习惯。“我们称它为我们幸福的家，而不是我们永远的家，”莉安说。“这是一个非常幸福的家，”莎拉同意。图片来源，Leanne 和 Sarah/BBC 图片说明，Leanne 和 Sarah 将他们共同购买的房子称为“幸福的家” 根据房主联盟的说法，与朋友一起购买房屋的好处包括更高的首付和预算以及分摊费用。但它表示，人们应该认真考虑潜在的陷阱，并通过提前了解自己的财务状况、寻求单独的法律建议并起草正式协议来提前做好计划。莎拉和莉安在搬入四年后以盈利的方式出售了他们的房子，他们将所积累的资产用于下一次单独的购买。“如果没有我们共同拥有的房产，我们谁都无法做到我们所做的事情，”莎拉说。 “这给我们带来了很多自由。”Leanne 认为她本来能够及时买得起她想要的东西，但与 Sarah 一起购买所带来的经济利益让这一切变得更快。“隐性单身税意味着，一切都需要花费更长的时间才能让你有能力做你想做的事情，”她补充道。他们的成功启发了他们的朋友 Philly 建立了 Cucoon——一个在线平台，为单身人士匹配可能一起购买的东西。她说，她的目标是“公平竞争环境”，并补充说，在住房方面，单身税特别高。如果你是单身，如何降低成本 将你的房地产货币化：出租房间、停车位和车库 共享晚餐：主人轮流用更大、更便宜的产品做饭 借贷圈子：一个人购买一件昂贵的物品，如割草机，然后将其传递出去 跑腿分摊：朋友们轮流开车去超市，分担燃油成本 朱莉娅·皮尔逊 (Julia Pearson)大约九年前，汉普郡建立了 Just4One 网站，当时她想去度假，发现如果她独自去，很多地方都会向她收取额外费用。除了对独身生活的实际支持外，该平台还列出了不包括单身附加费的旅行提供商。她说，单身感觉就像“一直审查您的费用”。在给司机的省钱技巧清单中，RAC 建议在您的汽车保险中添加指定司机。这是 Julia 尝试过的事情 - 并表示这为她节省了 8%。RAC 表示，这可以降低你的保费，但也警告说，这也可能起到相反的作用。朱莉娅还与朋友分享物品——她借了工具来翻修自己的家，还给人们从她的花园剪下的植物枝条。“我认为，作为一个社会，我们在分享和思考方面变得更加社交化。”与其思考“我必须出去买那个”，不如想想你还能怎么玩，除了必须买之外你还能做什么“这对社会方面也有好处，合二为一。”联系您 您是如何设法在生活的不同领域削减成本的？分享您的技巧获取我们的旗舰新闻通讯，其中包含您开始新的一天所需的所有头条新闻。在这里注册。

articles.title: Nicotine pouches can be marketed as 'lower risk' than cigarettes. Is that dangerous?
articles.summary: The FDA allowed some Zyn nicotine pouches to be marketed as "lower risk" than cigarettes. Public health experts agree they can help current smokers, but worry young people may become addicted.
articles.titleZh: 尼古丁袋可以被宣传为比香烟“风险更低”。那危险吗？
articles.summaryZh: FDA 允许一些 Zyn 尼古丁袋作为比香烟“风险更低”的产品进行销售。公共卫生专家一致认为，他们可以帮助当前的吸烟者，但担心年轻人可能会上瘾。

contentParagraphs.en: The FDA allowed some Zyn nicotine pouches to be marketed as "lower risk" than cigarettes.
contentParagraphs.zh: FDA 允许一些 Zyn 尼古丁袋作为比香烟“风险更低”的产品进行销售。

contentParagraphs.en: Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: 迈克尔·M·圣地亚哥/盖蒂图片社

contentParagraphs.en: Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: 迈克尔·M·圣地亚哥/盖蒂图片社

contentParagraphs.en: It comes in flavors like "Cool Mint," "Smooth" and "Chill." It's on the Ferrari F1 race car. And it's addictive.
contentParagraphs.zh: 它有“清凉薄荷”、“光滑”和“冰凉”等口味。它安装在法拉利 F1 赛车上。而且它很容易上瘾。

contentParagraphs.en: A paperclip-size pouch filled with bleach-white fibers and nicotine crystals, placed between the lip and gum, leeches nicotine and other chemicals into the user's bloodstream — allowing anyone to use nicotine discreetly.
contentParagraphs.zh: 一个回形针大小的小袋，里面装满了漂白剂白色纤维和尼古丁晶体，放置在嘴唇和牙龈之间，将尼古丁和其他化学物质吸进使用者的血液中，让任何人都可以谨慎地使用尼古丁。

contentParagraphs.en: One of the most popular brands of nicotine pouches, Zyn, got a boost from the Food and Drug Administration recently. The FDA authorized the company to advertise: "Using Zyn instead of cigarettes puts you at a lower risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis."
contentParagraphs.zh: Zyn 是最受欢迎的尼古丁袋装品牌之一，最近得到了美国食品和药物管理局的支持。 FDA授权该公司做广告：“使用Zyn代替香烟可以降低患口腔癌、心脏病、肺癌、中风、肺气肿和慢性支气管炎的风险。”

contentParagraphs.en: Bret Koplow, acting director of the FDA's Center for Tobacco Products, said in a press release that the decision "is intended to ensure that adult users have clear, science-based information about the relative harms of tobacco products, so they can make informed choices."
contentParagraphs.zh: FDA 烟草制品中心代理主任布雷特·科普洛 (Bret Koplow) 在一份新闻稿中表示，这一决定“旨在确保成年使用者对烟草制品的相对危害有清晰的、基于科学的信息，以便他们能够做出明智的选择。”

contentParagraphs.en: For the latest stories on the science of healthy living, subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
contentParagraphs.zh: 有关健康生活科学的最新故事，请订阅 NPR 的健康通讯。

contentParagraphs.en: Some public health researchers say that Zyn is a safer alternative to cigarettes and it can help curb the 480,000 or more U.S. deaths attributable to tobacco each year. But others also say it can be a gateway to riskier nicotine habits like smoking and hook people in adolescence.
contentParagraphs.zh: 一些公共卫生研究人员表示，Zyn 是一种比香烟更安全的替代品，它可以帮助遏制美国每年因烟草造成的 48 万或更多死亡人数。但其他人也表示，它可能成为吸烟等危险尼古丁习惯的门户，并让人们陷入青春期。

contentParagraphs.en: The case for Zyn
contentParagraphs.zh: Zyn 的案例

contentParagraphs.en: Nicotine is a drug extracted from the tobacco plant, though some companies use lab-made nicotine in their products.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尼古丁是从烟草植物中提取的药物，尽管一些公司在其产品中使用实验室制造的尼古丁。

contentParagraphs.en: Advocates of nicotine pouches emphasize their safety compared to cigarettes and other tobacco products that users burn. Mitch Zeller, a professor at Dartmouth Geisel School of Medicine and former director at the FDA's Center for Tobacco Products, says the pouches are "demonstrably less harmful than burning tobacco leaves and inhaling the 7,000 chemicals that are in tobacco smoke."
contentParagraphs.zh: 尼古丁袋的拥护者强调，与使用者燃烧的香烟和其他烟草产品相比，尼古丁袋的安全性。达特茅斯盖泽尔医学院教授、FDA 烟草产品中心前主任米奇·泽勒 (Mitch Zeller) 表示，这些烟袋“明显比燃烧烟叶和吸入烟草烟雾中的 7,000 种化学物质的危害要小”。

contentParagraphs.en: He says when it comes to heavy smokers who want to quit, it's a "no-brainer" to switch to nicotine pouches.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说，对于想要戒烟的重度吸烟者来说，改用尼古丁袋是“理所当然的”。

contentParagraphs.en: Zyn underscored that idea in an interview with NPR. Brian Erkkila, director of external affairs and head of scientific engagement for Zyn's parent company Philip Morris International, says Zyn helped him quit cigarettes and he wonders if it could have helped his father — who died from lung cancer — had it been available.
contentParagraphs.zh: Zyn 在接受 NPR 采访时强调了这一想法。 Zyn 母公司菲利普莫里斯国际公司 (Philip Morris International) 的对外事务总监兼科学参与主管 Brian Erkkila 表示，Zyn 帮助他戒烟，他想知道如果 Zyn 能够帮助他死于肺癌的父亲，是否也能有所帮助。

contentParagraphs.en: Still, Erkkila says "nicotine is addictive and is not risk-free."
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管如此，埃尔基拉表示“尼古丁会让人上瘾，而且并非没有风险。”

contentParagraphs.en: When it comes to nicotine pouches, Bonnie Halpern-Felsher, a professor of pediatrics at Stanford University, agrees they have "meaningful harm reduction potential" for current smokers. She notes risks may include heart issues, neurological and psychiatric illnesses and dental problems. It is too soon to know if nicotine pouches raise the risk of oral cancer.
contentParagraphs.zh: 谈到尼古丁袋，斯坦福大学儿科教授邦妮·哈尔彭-费尔舍 (Bonnie Halpern-Felsher) 同意，它们对当前吸烟者具有“有意义的减少危害的潜力”。她指出风险可能包括心脏问题、神经和精神疾病以及牙齿问题。现在判断尼古丁袋是否会增加患口腔癌的风险还为时过早。

contentParagraphs.en: "We don't know all the effects of these newer oral nicotine products," she says, explaining that it took over 50 years to fully understand the harmful effects of cigarettes. Zyn products have been around for about a decade in the U.S.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们不知道这些新型口服尼古丁产品的所有影响，”她说，并解释说，我们花了 50 多年的时间才完全了解香烟的有害影响。 Zyn 产品在美国已推出约十年。

contentParagraphs.en: Dr. Robert Jackler is a Stanford University professor emeritus who runs a research group on tobacco advertisements. He points out that Zyn and other nicotine pouches aren't approved smoking cessation tools, such as nicotine gum or patches. He also says Zyn's positioning with high-nicotine products, flavored products and relentless marketing runs counter to promoting cessation.
contentParagraphs.zh: 罗伯特·杰克勒博士是斯坦福大学名誉教授，负责管理一个烟草广告研究小组。他指出，Zyn 和其他尼古丁袋不是经批准的戒烟工具，例如尼古丁口香糖或尼古丁贴片。他还表示，Zyn 的高尼古丁产品、调味产品和无情的营销定位与促进戒烟背道而驰。

contentParagraphs.en: Jackler says names for flavors with words like "cool," "smooth" and "chill" work to promote Zyn "as a lifestyle enhancer." He adds that Zyn has advertisements with active people like mountain climbers and compares Zyn to coffee and alcohol — to "portray it as safe and healthy."
contentParagraphs.zh: Jackler 表示，带有“酷”、“顺滑”和“冰冷”等词语的口味名称有助于宣传 Zyn“作为生活方式的增强剂”。他补充说，Zyn 为登山者等活跃人士做广告，并将 Zyn 比作咖啡和酒精，“将其描绘成安全和健康的”。

contentParagraphs.en: In response, Erkkila told NPR that Philip Morris International is committed to responsible marketing and that they only target advertisements to adults. Erkkila also says a 3 mg Zyn delivers a "similar amount" of nicotine to a single cigarette and he doesn't necessarily consider 11 mg — Zyn's highest dose offering — a "high dose" as it is within the range of other available nicotine products.
contentParagraphs.zh: 对此，埃尔基拉告诉 NPR，菲利普莫里斯国际公司致力于负责任的营销，他们只针对成年人投放广告。 Erkkila 还表示，3 毫克 Zyn 与一支香烟的尼古丁含量“相似”，他并不一定认为 11 毫克（Zyn 的最高剂量产品）是“高剂量”，因为它在其他可用尼古丁产品的范围内。

contentParagraphs.en: Erkkila says the FDA's 2025 authorization specifically credited flavors with helping adult smokers try — and switch to — Zyn, since "you can't switch to a product unless you try it first."
contentParagraphs.zh: Erkkila 表示，FDA 2025 年的授权特别将口味归功于帮助成年吸烟者尝试并转向 Zyn，因为“除非先尝试，否则无法转向产品”。

contentParagraphs.en: Mary Hrywna, a professor at Rutgers School of Public Health, agreed that flavors may help adult tobacco users switch to nicotine pouches. But Hrywna and all the experts we spoke to say it should not be used by kids.
contentParagraphs.zh: 罗格斯大学公共卫生学院教授玛丽·赫里纳 (Mary Hrywna) 同意，口味可能有助于成年烟草使用者转向尼古丁袋装。但 Hrywna 和我们采访过的所有专家都表示，儿童不应该使用它。

contentParagraphs.en: The risks may outweigh the benefits "if kids start to use this product," Zeller says. If that happens, he notes the FDA may pull authorization.
contentParagraphs.zh: 泽勒说，“如果孩子们开始使用这个产品”，风险可能会超过好处。他指出，如果发生这种情况，FDA 可能会取消授权。

contentParagraphs.en: "That's not harm reduction," he says. "That's only increasing harm, regardless of how small the risk of a pouch is compared to a cigarette."
contentParagraphs.zh: “这并不是减少伤害，”他说。 “无论与香烟相比，烟袋的风险有多小，这只会增加危害。”

contentParagraphs.en: Adolescent use of Zyn
contentParagraphs.zh: 青少年使用 Zyn

contentParagraphs.en: A national survey by the FDA on tobacco use by young people found that less than 2% of teens used nicotine pouches, and that's been stable since 2022.
contentParagraphs.zh: FDA 对年轻人烟草使用情况进行的一项全国调查发现，只有不到 2% 的青少年使用尼古丁袋，并且自 2022 年以来一直保持稳定。

contentParagraphs.en: But another study did find more teens using the pouches. The long-running Monitoring the Future study from the University of Michigan found 12th-graders' lifetime use of nicotine pouches increased from 6.8% to 10.0%, between 2024 and 2025. The same study found 4.4% of 12th-graders in 2025 reported using nicotine pouches within the past 30 days.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但另一项研究确实发现有更多的青少年使用这些育儿袋。密歇根大学的长期监测未来研究发现，2024 年至 2025 年间，12 年级学生终生使用尼古丁袋的比例从 6.8% 增加到 10.0%。该研究发现，2025 年，4.4% 的 12 年级学生报告在过去 30 天内使用过尼古丁袋。

contentParagraphs.en: The number of teens saying they had tried using nicotine pouches has experts worried.
contentParagraphs.zh: 表示曾尝试使用尼古丁袋的青少年数量令专家们感到担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: Emily Hilliard, a senior press secretary for the Department of Health and Human Services, told NPR: "[the] FDA remains committed to preventing youth access to and use of tobacco products and continues to enforce the federal minimum age of 21 for the sale of all tobacco products." She also reiterated that "there is no safe tobacco product."
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国卫生与公共服务部高级新闻秘书艾米丽·希利亚德 (Emily Hilliard) 告诉 NPR：“FDA 仍然致力于防止青少年接触和使用烟草产品，并继续执行联邦销售所有烟草产品的最低年龄为 21 岁的规定。”她还重申“不存在安全的烟草产品”。

contentParagraphs.en: Halpern-Felsher says schools find evidence of nicotine pouch use as litter, and they are easy for students to conceal and hard for schools to police. Her lab publishes a curriculum for adole
contentParagraphs.zh: Halpern-Felsher 说，学校发现了尼古丁袋被用作垃圾的证据，学生很容易隐藏它们，但学校很难监管。她的实验室出版了阿多课程
